item.title: Operation Hermes: VAT fraud 450 mln, seizures 11 mln
item.description: ## TL;DR - Six precautionary measures and seizures totaling approximately 11 million - VAT fraud in electronics and IT - 93 companies in the Italian part of the investigation
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Six precautionary measures and seizures worth approximately 11 million - VAT fraud in electronics and IT - 93 companies in the Italian part of the investigation - Approximately 300 searches in eight European countries
## Key facts - Operation → “Hermes” - Investigation → alleged VAT carousel fraud - Sector → trade in electronic and IT products - Precautionary measures → six people - Seizures → approximately 11 million euros - Invoices deemed false → more than 450 million euros - Period → 2022-2025 - Searches → approximately 300 in eight European countries
The Guardia di Finanza of Varese carried out six personal precautionary measures and seized assets and sums of money worth approximately 11 million euros. The operation, conducted as part of “Hermes”, forms part of an investigation into an alleged criminal association aimed at committing tax fraud, aggravated by its transnational dimension.
At the heart of the investigation is the alleged VAT carousel fraud in the trade of electronic and IT products. The alleged scheme is believed to have developed across several European Union countries; the investigative activities were entrusted to the Economic and Financial Police Unit of Varese, with the cooperation of the Milan Pef Unit.
Coordination is entrusted to the Milan and Palermo offices of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office, known by the acronym EPPO. The judge for preliminary investigations at the Milan Court ordered precautionary measures against six people: two, reportedly domiciled in Rome, were taken to prison; one was placed under house arrest in the province of Bergamo; the other three were subjected to a residence requirement in the provinces of Salerno and Rome.
### The measures and the seizure
A preventive seizure order, also on an equivalent-value basis, was added to the personal measures. The order concerned assets, valuables and financial resources attributable to eight suspects and three companies involved, for a total value of approximately 11 million euros.
The source therefore distinguishes between two aspects of the operation: on the one hand, the personal measures ordered by the Milan judge; on the other, the preventive order concerning assets, valuables and money traceable to the individuals and companies identified. Both measures were carried out as part of the same operation by the Guardia di Finanza of Varese, with the contribution of the Milan Pef Unit and under the coordination of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office.
The allegation described by investigators has a transnational dimension because the alleged VAT mechanism was reconstructed across several European Union countries. The source places the investigation in the electronics and IT trade and indicates the involvement of several European Union states. The measures carried out in Italy include the precautionary measures against individuals and the seizure of assets, valuables and money up to the stated threshold. According to the Guardia di Finanza's reconstruction, 93 companies operating in the provinces of Bergamo, Milan, Rome, Salerno, Como and Brescia are involved in the Italian part of the investigation. Between 2022 and 2025, the total value of the invoices deemed false exceeded 450 million euros. These figures refer to the Italian component of the investigation into the alleged VAT fraud scheme.
### From the Italian part to the European network
The investigation is part of a broader operation, carried out simultaneously in several European countries and coordinated by EPPO's central office in Luxembourg. Overall, approximately 300 searches were carried out in eight European countries: Spain, Malta, Portugal, France, Austria, the Netherlands and Germany, in addition to Italy.
The international dimension concerns not only the number of countries involved. The Guardia di Finanza explains that the alleged mechanism relies on the VAT-exemption regime provided for trade between European Union countries. A fictitious company, called a «shell company» or a «missing trader», is inserted between companies from different countries.
The shell company sources its goods from an EU supplier without VAT being applied to the purchase, then resells the goods to an Italian company, charging VAT at the standard rate. However, the VAT collected would not be paid to the Treasury: the shell company would sell the goods below cost without paying the tax shown on the invoices.
Investigators generally describe these companies as lacking operational structures and employees, often registered in the names of nominees. Their operations would cease after a relatively short period, to be replaced by other companies with similar characteristics.
### Steps in the carousel
The scheme may include additional stages through companies known as «filter» or «buffer» companies. These businesses are inserted into the commercial chain with the aim of making it more difficult to identify the mechanism and the ultimate beneficiaries.
At the final stage of the chain are the «broker» companies, genuinely operating businesses that purchase the products with VAT charged and consequently accrue a credit with the Treasury. The goods can then be placed on the Italian market at prices made artificially competitive by the mechanism or resold abroad, including to the companies from which the first transaction had originated. This is how the so-called «carousel» can restart.
According to investigators, the damage to public finances stems from the VAT shown on the shell companies' invoices: the tax is collected in subsequent commercial transactions, but is not paid to the Treasury. The international coordination of the “Hermes” operation involved the offices of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office in Madrid, Porto, Milan, Palermo, Paris, Graz, Valletta, Bucharest, Rotterdam, Frankfurt and Vilnius. The operation therefore brought together EPPO structures located in several countries, alongside the work carried out in Italy by the Varese Guardia di Finanza and the Milan Pef Unit.
The operation benefited from the support of Europol, law enforcement agencies and tax authorities in the countries concerned. The activities extended to the homes, company premises and offices of natural and legal persons considered, for various reasons, to be linked to the alleged fraudulent scheme. During the action, precautionary measures, searches and seizures were carried out.
For the Italian part, funds held at Swiss banks were also seized. The reference to accounts in Switzerland therefore falls within the asset-related activities carried out as part of the investigation, together with the assets, valuables and money already traced back to the eight suspects and the three companies covered by the preventive seizure order.
### The profile of the investigation
The Guardia di Finanza places the operation within the framework of actions against VAT fraud, tax evasion and economic and financial crime. Investigators explain that phenomena of this kind can undermine free competition and penalize businesses that operate in compliance with the rules.
The same account retains the alleged nature of the charges. The persons involved were subject to the measures as part of the investigation, while responsibility must be definitively established in court. This is the step indicated by the source for the judicial follow-up of the case.
The operation thus brings together an Italian investigative component, with operating companies identified in various provinces, and activity coordinated at European level. The searches, seizures and measures carried out in the various countries were conducted as part of the same operation against the alleged carousel VAT fraud scheme.

item.title: Kastritis: difficult moment will help us grow, maximum confidence in the group
item.description: Varese loses his Champions League debut in Murcia against UCAM Murcia, with the absences of McDowell and Della Valle; Kastritis highlights the defensive intensity and confidence in the group, next game in three days.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Varese loses its cup debut in Murcia - Kastritis promotes defensive intensity - McDowell and Della Valle are significant absences - Librizzi: the team can do much better
## Key facts - Debut → Champions League - Place → Murcia - Teams → Pallacanestro Varese and UCAM Murcia - Coaches → Ioannis Kastritis and Sito Alonso - Absences → McDowell and Della Valle - Playmaker → Matteo Librizzi - Next match → a new match in three days
### The coach's reading Murcia gave Pallacanestro Varese a first cup match to forget. The red and white team was overwhelmed by UCAM Murcia, while coach Ioannis Kastritis chose to start with compliments to his opponents, recognizing coach Alonso and the Murcia team for a great performance.
However, in the results of the Varese match, Kastritis saved the work done in the defensive half of the pitch. According to the coach, the players gave their all, especially in the defensive phase, with many very aggressive elements ready to fight for every ball. The evaluation concerns the attitude shown during the match, even if it does not erase the debut defeat.
The coach described Varese as a group of players who work hard every day. The team is new and still has to build its mechanisms, growing possession after possession. The construction of the group is therefore indicated as a path that is still open, to be developed through daily work and the experience accumulated in matches.
Kastritis recognized the weight of the absences of McDowell and Della Valle, defined as "a significant factor". At the same time, he reiterated that Varese Basketball does not want and will not make excuses. The coach's position is clear: training difficulties and absences are part of the situation, but must not become a justification for the performance offered.
Even criticism, according to Kastritis, is normal and right at this moment. However, they must have a concrete utility and be productive, so as to push the team out of their comfort zone. The coach accompanied this request with a declaration of full confidence in each of his players, keeping the focus of the discussion on the group and the work to be completed. ### The reactions after the race Matteo Librizzi indicated the analysis of errors as the first step after the defeat in Murcia. The Varese basketball point guard explained that the team must fully understand what didn't work, because the approach to the first match of the tournament was not the desired one. His assessment therefore concerns the start of the match and the way in which the group approached their debut in the Champions League.
Librizzi did not hide his self-criticism, but linked the analysis to the possibility of reacting already in the next matches. The team, he said, is "perfectly aware that it can do much better." The goal indicated by the point guard is to work to identify errors and transform that reading into an immediate improvement in subsequent games.
On the UCAM Murcia side, Sito Alonso described a positive evening for the team's first home victory in the Champions League. The coach attributed the result to the intensity with which Murcia approached the match and the desire to limit the main offensive points of reference of the Varese team. The preparation for the match therefore focused on the attacking solutions considered most important for Varese.
Alonso also highlighted the return to the pitch of Kaiser Gates, who was absent due to a very long and serious injury. The coach chose to give him space at the start of the match to allow him to find his rhythm. The response from a physical point of view was considered positive, so much so that Alonso defined recovery as a fundamental element for Murcia.
The UCAM coach recalled that he knew Varese well and that the Italian team lacked high-level players. However, he specified that Murcia also had to deal with the absence of key elements. The reading of the opponents therefore did not stop at the red and white difficulties, but also considered the situation of the Spanish team.
For Alonso, in the Champions League the points difference has a decisive impact on the group. Hence the request to maintain constant defensive aggression for the entire 40 minutes, without drops. His explanation distinguishes two behaviors: when Murcia is not aggressive it becomes vulnerable; when he manages to impose his physicality, he can compete with anyone. ### The work indicated by Kastritis The message addressed to Varese Basketball already looks to the continuation of the season. Kastritis defined the period the team went through as difficult, but added that in the future it could be considered extremely valuable for the growth of the group. The current difficulty is therefore inserted into a broader path, without separating it from the work necessary to improve.
The condition indicated by the coach is to all remain united and solid. The work must continue every day, with a double objective: improving individual players and helping the team as a whole grow. Kastritis did not separate the two dimensions, because in his message individual and collective development proceed together.
The coach also rejected the idea of ​​immediate perfection. Expecting to already be perfect in October, he explained, would be unrealistic. The defeat doesn't make him happy, but his assessment looks at the ability to face difficulties by remaining united and building the path day after day.
The next match is already indicated shortly: a new match awaits Varese in three days. Kastritis linked this commitment to the need to remain united and continue pushing, without interrupting the work started. The calendar therefore offers the team an immediate opportunity to apply what emerged from the words of the coach and point guard.
### A season of ups and downs Kastritis recalled that the story of a season is made up of high and low moments. The point, in his perspective, is not to ignore the negative phase or declare oneself satisfied after a defeat. It's about facing difficulties with unity, maintaining faith in the players and continuing to build the path.
The follow-up indicated to Pallacanestro Varese therefore remains linked to three recurring words in the coach's statements: unity, work and growth. The match in Murcia opened a difficult moment, but the response required does not involve excuses or promises. It goes from daily work, from the analysis of errors and from the ability to remain solid in view of the next commitment.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/kastritis-momento-difficile-ci-aiutera-a-crescere-massima-fiducia-nel-gruppo/2701573/)*

item.title: Pro patria beats Varese 5-2 in the Coppa Italia
item.description: ## TL;DR - Pro Patria beats Varese 5-2 at Franco Ossola. - Maistrello, Mapelli and Bonaidi seal the first 3-0. - Gallotti and Castellucchio bring back
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Pro Patria beats Varese 5-2 at the Franco Ossola. - Maistrello, Mapelli and Bonaidi make it 3-0. - Gallotti and Castellucchio bring Varese back to 2-3. - In the round of 32, Pro will face Leon.
## Key facts - → Pro Patria Result 5, Varese 2 - → Franco Ossola Stadium, Masnago - Serie D Italian → Cup Competition - Next round → Sixteenth against Leon - Opening hours → Wednesday at 3pm - Last Derby → 14 March 2010
Varese tried, but Pro Patria did not forgive Franco Ossola. The tigers won 5-2 in Masnago, winning the passage to the sixteenth round of the Italian Cup Series D, where they will face Leon. The race produced many nets, but also an obvious difference in the quality of the roses and in the concreteness under the goal.
### The advantage built in the first half
The first half showed two distinct attitudes. Varese tried to take advantage of the restarts and built some interesting plots, while Pro Patria appeared more maneuvering. To see the first conclusion it was necessary to wait for the 12': Favale engaged Gnonto with a left-handed man from outside, rejected in a dive by the tigrotto goalkeeper. The Pro responded with a head shot of Maistrello finished over the crossbar and with a crossbar of Nanni neutralized on the ground by Mangano.
At 20' the red-whites had the sharpest opportunity of the first part. Del Señor hit a nice corner, Sovogui stretched the head ball and Dodaj, stationed in the goal area, sent a high breath. Four minutes later De Ponti, in an attempt to get ahead of Maistrello on a Bonaidi cross, risked the own goal. From the next action, on the developments of the corner, Maistrello could not turn Nanni's cross towards the door.
The striker came back in 26', unlocking the challenge with a left-handed man of first intention who beat Mangano. The double came in the 31st minute, when Mapelli found the detour under goal, celebrating the former's classic goal. The double disadvantage did not stop Varese, who continued to look for the play in the last meters. At 42' Cogliati twisted the left-handed man; shortly after Favale, from a good position, did not frame the door with his right. In the recovery Mapelli and then Cannistrà rejected the off-white initiatives, sending the teams to the interval with the Pro Patria ahead 2-0. ## The second half and the derby context
The second half quickly changed the score. Varese started with greater initiative and came close to risking an own goal when Cannistrà misplaced a pass to Gnonto. The goalkeeper came out, and the ball went out for a corner after grazing the post. The corner led to another dangerous situation, with the ball bouncing in the area, but once again the red-and-whites lacked the decisive finish.
### From 3-0 to 3-2
Pro Patria reacted in the most effective way possible. On the counterattack, Bonaidi beat Mangano with a shot from the heart of the area, putting the Tigrotti 3-0 up. Varese did not give up and, at 10' in the second half, coach Ciceri brought on Castellucchio for Tronci and Gallotti for Sovogui.
The substitution paid off immediately. Gallotti scored with the first ball he touched: Gnonto misplaced a pass, Favale intercepted it and set up the young forward, who scored with a diagonal left-footed shot. The goal narrowed the gap and put the red-and-whites back in the match. Varese continued to push; Castellucchio then scored the temporary 2-3 with a wayward cross, reopening the contest even further.
The teams had lined up in different formations. Varese had opted for a 4-3-3, with Del Signore as the playmaker alongside Malinverno and Piantoni, while Favale, Sovogui and Cogliati played up front. Zironelli responded with a 3-4-3, with Nanni, Maistrello and Siega leading the attack. The red-and-white comeback highlighted Pro Patria's lapse in concentration after the third goal, but Varese's efforts fell short of completing the comeback.
### A derby returning after sixteen years
The match in Masnago also marked the derby's return after sixteen years. The last meeting had been on 14 March 2010, when Sannino's team had beaten the blue-and-whites coached by the late Vincenzo Cosco 3-1. Varese would then be promoted to Serie B at the end of the season, while Pro Patria would end the campaign with a bitter relegation. More than 6000 days have passed since then, marked by the ups and downs of the two clubs, with promotions and bankruptcies along the way.
The historic occasion, however, did not have a fitting setting. The kickoff scheduled for 15:00 on Wednesday, during working hours, and the inability to buy tickets in person left the Franco Ossola almost empty: there were about one hundred fans in the grandstand, while a dozen occupied the away section. The source describes the ticket-sales policy as in need of review and observes that a match between two historic rivals was reduced to a show for a select few. ## What happens after 5-2
### The ending that set the result
After Varese's 2-3, the match remained open until stoppage time, but the red-and-white push did not come to fruition. Late on, Pro Patria first extended its lead with Gianola's penalty, awarded for De Ponti's hold on Frattini. Shortly afterward, Frattini himself put the match to bed: he stole the ball from De Ponti and scored the goal that made it 5-2, the final score.
The double incident completed a match in which Pro Patria knew how to strike at decisive moments. Varese had reopened the game after trailing by three goals, but failed to turn the comeback into a positive result. For the tigrotti, on the other hand, the victory means progressing to the next round of the Coppa Italia di Serie D.
### The Coppa makes way for the league
With the Coppa Italia interlude over, Pro Patria will face Leon in the round of 32. The match played at Franco Ossola was the round-of-64 tie and represented the first knockout fixture before the two teams' league double-header. The next Coppa stage is therefore already set, although the source does not indicate the date of the match.
For Varese, the return to league action will once again be at Franco Ossola, where Oltrepò will arrive. The red-and-white team will have to try to turn the page after the defeat in Crema and the one suffered against Pro Patria. The next home fixture will thus mark the transition from the knockout competition to the need to get the league campaign back on track.
Pro Patria, meanwhile, will be at the Speroni against Sant'Angelo. The stated objective is to try to close the gap on Pistoiese, who on the same day showed that they are not unbeatable by losing at home to Sestri Levante. Pistoiese's result therefore opens up a different outlook for the tigrotti's campaign, as they are called to continue the league after advancing in the Coppa.
The schedule therefore sends both teams toward a new home fixture, but with different opponents and objectives: Varese will host Oltrepò to respond to its last two defeats, while Pro Patria will welcome Sant'Angelo with an eye on the gap to Pistoiese. The Masnago clash thus ends 5-2, but for the two rivals the league starts again immediately.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/il-varese-ci-prova-la-pro-patria-pero-non-perdona-5-2-tigrotto-al-franco-ossola/2700043/)*

## TL;DR - The 26-27 motor skills project gets underway in Luvinate - The school is collaborating with the Varese Basket School - The program is aimed at children in Nursery School - Sport and play support psychophysical and social development
## Key facts - What: motor activity project - Where: Luvinate Nursery School - When: project 26-27 - Collaboration: Varese Basket School - Recipients: Preschool children - Activities: basketball, ball, coordination and spatio-temporal orientation
### The project in Luvinate In Luvinate, the 26-27 motor activity project of the Kindergarten School began, carried out in collaboration with the Varese Basket School. The initiative is aimed at kindergarten children and renews and strengthens the school's commitment to the healthy growth of its young pupils.
Sport plays a central role in the proposal and contributes to the psychophysical and social growth of children already in the early years. The school thus integrates movement into the educational path, instead of limiting it to a leisure parenthesis.
The project aims to offer children a structured but playful space for movement. The choice is linked to sedentary lifestyle, described in the source as an early educational challenge. The response identified by the Kindergarten of Luvinate is an activity organized through play, but maintaining a size suitable for children.
With the accompaniment of the qualified instructors of the Varese Basket School, children experience the first elements of basketball and test their motor skills. The proposal includes exercises with the ball, paths for coordination and activities dedicated to orientation in space and time.
The start of the project therefore combines collaboration with a sports reality with the daily life of the Nursery School. The expected result of the school is a path in which play and movement accompany the growth of children, with attention to both the physical and social components. ## The educational value of sport ### Body, relationships and autonomy In the 3-to-6 age group, physical activity is described as a genuine educational tool. The project of the Luvinate Nursery School starts from this approach and combines physical development with a series of objectives related to personal growth and relationships among children.
The program stems from the joint work of the teachers in Luvinate and the professionals from the Varese Basket School and aims to develop body awareness, inclusion and socialization. The proposal also seeks to strengthen self-esteem and autonomy through movement and play experiences in early childhood.
According to the source, the value of the initiative is not limited to learning the first sports techniques. Early movement is identified as a key to preventing postural problems and promoting an active lifestyle, which the children are intended to maintain into adulthood as well.
The project thus brings together the contribution of the teachers and that of the qualified instructors. On the one hand, there is the school, with its educational role; on the other, the Varese Basket School, which brings sports expertise and offers activities related to basketball, the ball, coordination and orientation. The stated aim is to provide 360-degree stimulation.
“We are happy about this collaboration,” says the educational team, which believes that Nursery School should provide 360-degree stimulation. The thanks go to the Varese Basket School and the other sports organizations, which during this year will offer the young pupils opportunities for play and growth.
In the educational team's comment, the collaboration is therefore included in a broader offering of opportunities for play and growth. The Varese Basket School is thanked together with the other sports organizations that, over the course of this year, will help provide the children with additional stimulation. ## From basic techniques to play experiences ### Project activities The program launched in Luvinate takes shape through activities in which basketball represents one of the first sports experiences offered to the children. The qualified instructors from Varese Basket School guide them in learning the basic techniques, keeping the work within a playful setting.
Alongside basketball fundamentals, the program includes exploring motor skills. The ball becomes one of the tools used during the activities, while coordination exercises allow the children to experiment with movement. Spatial-temporal orientation activities are also planned, included in the program together with the other physical activities.
This structure makes it possible to present the project not as a lesson focused on a single discipline, but as a set of physical experiences intended for the children of the Preschool. Basketball remains the focus of the collaboration, while play, the ball, coordination and orientation constitute the means through which the children can explore their abilities.
The continuation indicated by the school also covers the rest of the year. The message from the educational team recalls that, in addition to Varese Basket School, other sports organizations will offer the children opportunities for play and growth. The source does not indicate which organizations these are, but places them within the educational program aimed at the young pupils.
The 26-27 project therefore presents itself as a structured, play-based physical activity, led by qualified instructors and integrated into the life of Luvinate's Preschool. The planned experiences include both an introduction to basketball and work on motor skills through the ball, coordination and spatial-temporal orientation. For the children, the program offers opportunities for play and growth, while for the school it represents the renewal of a commitment to healthy development in early childhood.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/sport-alla-materna-a-luvinate-al-via-il-progetto-motorio-in-collaborazione-con-la-varese-basket-school/2700754/)*

item.description: ## In brief - Two cultural events at Varese on 9 and 11 October - Dante at the centre of Friday's meeting at 5:30 pm - Three unpublished stories by Carlo
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Two cultural events in Varese on 9 and 11 October - Dante at the center of Friday's meeting at 5:30 pm - Three unpublished stories by Carlo Linati on Sunday at 5:00 pm
## Key facts - → Villa Recalcati headquarters, Piazzale Libertà 1, Varese - Friday, October 9, 5:30 pm → One hundred questions to Dante and one hundred answers - Sunday, October 11, 5:00 p.m. → The day of the confrontation and other stories - First volume Hephaestus → Editions - Second volume → GaEle Publisher
### The first meeting Varese hosts the double literary event with which the Storytelling Festival enters the heart of the programming. Next weekend, the headquarters of Villa Recalcati, in Piazzale Libertà 1, will be the site of two meetings dedicated to dialogue with the great classics and the rediscovery of Lombard literary heritage.
The first date is Friday, October 9, at 5:30 pm. The program includes the presentation of "One hundred questions to Dante and one hundred answers", a volume published by Edizioni Efesto and written by Giorgio Gibertini and Paolo Velonà.
The work is constructed as an impossible interview with the Supreme Poet. Its architecture recalls that of the Divine Comedy and entrusts Dante with answers on current issues, expressed through an alternation of modern language and ancient triplets. The setting thus combines the Dantean figure with questions related to contemporary life, maintaining the reference to the ancient poetic form.
In the course of the work, universal and contemporary themes enter. These include anger management, raising children, the possibility of a just war, and overcoming fear. The text also addresses curiosities about happiness and school, up to the invention of cinema.
During the afternoon Giorgio Gibertini will talk with Carla Soresina. The presentation focuses on the book signed by Gibertini and Velonà and the choice to have Dante answer questions related to current affairs, following the structure of the Divine Comedy. ## The unpublished works of Carlo Linati
### A handcrafted publication The second appointment of the Festival del Racconto is scheduled for Sunday, October 11th at 5:00 PM. For the occasion, the protagonist will be «La giornata del rinfaccio e altri racconti», published by GaEle Editore and presented as a precious volume entirely handcrafted by the publishing house from Cuvio.
The Sunday event will be the opportunity to present three unpublished short stories by Carlo Linati. The texts were discovered by his niece Bianca Maria Mora Pina and by Mario Chiodetti, noted as a scholar of the famous writer. The discovery brings never-before-published material by the Como-born author into the publication and forms the core of the meeting dedicated to the volume.
The publication turns the spotlight back on a writer deeply linked to Lombardy. The profile outlined by the program brings together innovative writing and a passion for nature and the culture of the region. These are the traits through which the book is included in the part of the Festival dedicated to the rediscovery of Lombard literary heritage.
At the event, Mario Chiodetti will engage in a discussion with Cesare Chiericati and Mauro Novelli. The program therefore adds to the presentation of the three stories a discussion with two interlocutors presented alongside the scholar who found the texts together with Bianca Maria Mora Pina.
The title chosen by GaEle Editore, the entirely handcrafted production of the volume, and the recovery of the never-before-published stories define the character of the second date. The source in fact connects the rediscovery of Carlo Linati to his relationship with Lombardy, with nature, and with the culture of the region, offering a new opportunity to bring the author back to the center of literary attention. ## The continuation of the programming
### The dates of the festival The continuation of the initiative is already marked in the calendar of the Festival del Racconto: two separate meetings, concentrated on the weekend and hosted at the same venue of Villa Recalcati, at Piazzale Libertà 1 in Varese. The sequence connects the first appointment dedicated to Dante with the subsequent one dedicated to the unpublished works of Carlo Linati.
The first stage is set for Friday, October 9th at 5:30 PM. The event program indicates the presentation of 'Cento domande a Dante e cento risposte', published by Edizioni Efesto and written by Giorgio Gibertini and Paolo Velonà. A dialogue between Giorgio Gibertini and Carla Soresina is scheduled for this meeting.
The second stage arrives on Sunday, October 11th at 5:00 PM. The calendar lists the presentation of 'La giornata del rinfaccio e altri racconti', published by GaEle Editore. The volume includes three unpublished stories by Carlo Linati, while the appointment features a discussion between Mario Chiodetti, Cesare Chiericati, and Mauro Novelli.
The two dates make up the double cultural appointment announced by the Festival. The program combines a reinterpretation of the figure of the Supreme Poet, constructed through current questions and the structure of the Divine Comedy, with the rediscovery of never-published materials by an author linked to Lombardy.
The venue and the times therefore remain the common reference for both presentations: Villa Recalcati for both meetings, 5:30 PM for the volume dedicated to Dante, and 5:00 PM for the one dedicated to Carlo Linati. The Festival weekend thus unfolds between a literary dialogue with the great classic and the recovery of three stories that remained unpublished.

## TL;DR - On Sunday, October 11, Agrivarese comes to Angera's lakeside promenade - The event will be open from 9 to 19 - More than 40 businesses, animals and tastings are on the program - Organized by the Chamber of Commerce and the Municipality of Angera
## Key facts - Event → Agrivarese by the lake - Date → Sunday, October 11 - Location → Angera lakeside promenade - Time → from 9 to 19 - Registered businesses → 42 - Organizers → Camera di Commercio di Varese and Comune di Angera
### The event on Lake Maggiore The second edition in 2026 of the Varese agricultural fair will bring Agrivarese to Lake Maggiore: on Sunday, October 11, the Angera lakeside promenade will host the event from 9 to 19.
The event is organized by the Camera di Commercio di Varese and the Comune di Angera, together with trade associations in the agricultural sector. The program combines agricultural businesses with animals, workshops for children, tastings and a conference dedicated to the mountains. The aim is to promote local agricultural production and encourage families, children and young people to become familiar with the world and professions of agriculture.
The event also supports the idea that the local area should consume what it produces. According to the organizers, shortening the distance between production and consumption means reducing transportation and energy consumption, as well as protecting green spaces and local traditions. Agrivarese is therefore presented as a day dedicated to local products and learning about agricultural activities.
The president of the Camera di Commercio di Varese, Mauro Vitiello, explained that the return to Angera brings several new features, some of which had already been presented in this year's editions. He described Agrivarese as a fair, but also as a way of representing the area's agriculture and bringing it closer to the people who live there, as well as to guests from farther afield.
In his remarks, Vitiello highlighted the value of zero-kilometer products and the need to make the quality of the produce recognizable, from honey to other agricultural products. He also thanked the staff of the Camera di Commercio, the associations involved, the mayor of Angera and the municipal administration for making the initiative possible. The twice-yearly format, he added, following the initial reservations about its possible impact on the public, is considered a course worth pursuing. ## An event linked to Angera's history
### The livestock show and the agricultural past The mayor of Angera, Marcella Androni, gave a positive assessment of the event and thanked the Chamber of Commerce. In her remarks, she also mentioned councilor Christian Marzetta, who worked on organizing the event with responsibility for culture, and Navigazione, which made services between Angera and Arona available every half hour that day.
The lake connection was presented by the mayor as a sign of unity between two regions and two cities. Androni also explained that the autumn setting on the lakeside promenade suits the event: the space is suitable for the event and allows the area's agri-food production to be displayed.
For the mayor, Agrivarese evokes a tradition already rooted in local history. The initiative is in fact linked to the livestock show organized in the last century by the Municipality and agricultural associations, a day when local products were brought and displayed. Promoting those products also serves to shorten the supply chain and bring agricultural work back into public awareness.
Androni observed that, in the current situation, agricultural work could offer greater satisfaction than other activities. She also recalled that until the 1950s, agriculture was one of the pillars of the city's economy. The historical reference dates back to 1497, when Ludovico il Moro granted Angera city status, mainly so that it could have a market and two agricultural exhibitions.
Anna Deligios, secretary general of the Varese Chamber of Commerce, described Agrivarese as an established format. As she explained, attendees look for farm animals, performances, the mycological exhibition and, above all, the agricultural businesses present.
For this edition, 42 agricultural businesses have registered. In the Varese edition, Deligios recalled, with a caveat about her memory, there were 34. The Chamber of Commerce interprets this figure as a sign of the appeal that Angera's venue also has for agricultural businesses. The presence of the businesses therefore remains the central point of an event that brings together local products, civic memory and direct contact with the public. ## Schools, local products and activities along the lakeside
### What's new in the program Among the announced new features is collaboration with some schools. The students have designed a striking installation, an arch intended to symbolically represent the entrance to the event. The Chamber of Commerce highlighted the value of bringing together young people studying agriculture and farming businesses.
There will also be sessions presenting local products curated by Associazione Viticoltori Varesini, Consorzio di tutela della Formaggella del Luinese and Consorzio Qualità Miele Varesino. The sessions have limited capacity, with a maximum of 25 people each; registration and information are available on the event website.
Local dishes will be offered by producers from Mercato Coperto di Varese together with several local associations: Associazione Canottieri De Bastiani, Comitato genitori di Angera, Amici della Bruschera, Gruppo Alpini di Angera and Associazione Gido Mobiglia Onlus, which will organize the chestnut festival.
Another area will be dedicated to the Gluten Free Point. The organizers' stated aim is to discuss gluten-free products and the difficulties faced by those looking for a restaurant with a specific offering and processes capable of preventing contamination.
The Schools Area, designed for young people interested in entering the agricultural workforce, will allow them to engage with the agricultural vocational institute in Lesa, the training agency of the Province of Varese and the Newton institute. A gravel ride starting from Angera and following a route through scenic locations is also planned; places are limited for this activity too.
The day will also retain the elements that, according to the Chamber of Commerce, characterize the format: farm animals, performances, the mycological exhibition and farms. Tastings and a conference dedicated to the mountains will also be added. In terms of connections, Navigazione has scheduled Angera-Arona services every half hour for Sunday, complementing the lakeside event with a connection between the two cities.

Instead of remaining concentrated on the motorway, the traffic spilled onto the state road, shifting the pressure onto the road connection between the centers mentioned in the report. The sequence described is clear: first the tailback on the motorway, then the transfer of traffic onto the state road and, finally, a further slowdown at the point regulated by the traffic light.
The most critical point was in fact the bridge on the main ordinary road. The line already began at Castronno cemetery and reached approximately one kilometer, according to the description of the situation.

item.title: Cross-border grape harvest workers: 15 francs an hour
item.description: ## TL;DR - Around 50 cross-border commuters bring the grape harvest to life in Mendrisiotto - They come mainly from the province of Varese - Pay is around 15 net francs
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Around 50 cross-border workers take part in the grape harvest in the Mendrisiotto - They come mainly from the province of Varese - Pay is around 15 net francs per hour - The harvest usually lasts a month and a half
## Key facts - Who → about 50 cross-border workers - Origin → mainly the province of Varese - Activities → grape harvesting and loading - Harvesting → contract usually lasting a month and a half - Vineyard work → employment from April to November - Workdays → from three to seven or eight hours - Pay → about 15 net francs per hour - Age → from 18 to 70 years old
About fifty workers, mostly from the province of Varese, come to Ticino every autumn to take part in the grape harvest on the hills of Mendrisiotto. They are cross-border workers engaged in two distinct activities: grape harvesting and loading. Their number makes visible a seasonal presence that is renewed year after year, with a stable core and a turnover of new arrivals.
The work thus brings together those who join for the shorter phase and those who remain throughout the entire vineyard cycle. It is not a homogeneous group in terms of age, experience or length of commitment: the grape harvest brings new applicants and established returnees together in the same field.
### Two durations for the same work
The duration is not the same for everyone. For those who harvest grapes, the seasonal contract usually lasts a month and a half. Those who follow the entire vineyard work cycle, on the other hand, work from April to November. The workday also varies according to the needs of the field: it ranges from quick three-hour shifts to more demanding seven- or eight-hour sessions. The stated pay is about fifteen net francs per hour. The hourly figure can be explored in more detail in simulatore busta paga.
Putting the team together requires connections. Alongside the «hard core» of veterans who faithfully return every year, applications arrive via CV in Ticino. The turnover is about ten new people each season, and the workers’ ages range from 18 to 70.
The personal stories show the group’s variety. Maurizio spent 43 years in a factory as a lithographer and, as a retiree, considers the vineyard an experience capable of rejuvenating him. Matteo, 52, from Varese, works in the vineyard from April to November: he has fifteen seasons in Ticino and twenty-seven in total behind him. In his view, in the past the grape harvest had a more festive atmosphere, whereas today it seems more industrial and lacking in warmth. ## TL;DR - Egyptian 21-year-old arrested in Como - Theft targeting tourists on via per Cernobbio - Scuffle near the Lido di Villa Olmo - Investigations opened into the accomplice who fled
## Key facts - Charge: improper robbery - Arrested: 21-year-old Egyptian national - Intervention: Como Mobile Radio Section and Como-Rebbio Station - Stolen property: clothing, personal belongings and identity documents - Destination: Como Detention Centre
### The operation in Como During the night, on Via per Cernobbio, an attempt to steal belongings from a couple of tourists escalated into a violent scuffle, during which kicks and punches were thrown. The incident led to the arrest, by the Carabinieri of the Como Mobile Radio Section and the Como-Rebbio Station, of a 21-year-old Egyptian national, unlawfully present in the country, accused of improper robbery.
The incident began inside a van parked along the road, where the owners, a husband and wife, were sleeping. A loud noise suddenly woke them. The man, immediately noticing that some clothing and personal belongings were missing, contacted the Single Emergency Number 112.
The interception took place near the Lido di Villa Olmo: the theft victim and a passing motorist, identified as a witness, managed to do so. Once they had been reached, the two fugitives attacked them with kicks and punches in an attempt to evade capture.
One of the accomplices disappeared by climbing over the facility’s gate; the other, the 21-year-old, was pinned to the ground by the two men and held until the prompt arrival of the Carabinieri officers.
The transition from theft to the scuffle occurred during the escape, after the victim and the witness had reached the suspects. The husband was the person who had noticed the missing items and called 112; the other man involved in the interception was the passing motorist identified as the witness. ## The recovered stolen goods The recovery of the stolen goods took place in two distinct stages, both described after the young man was stopped. During the subsequent search, the officers found a bag on the 21-year-old containing the goods stolen from the woman. The first discovery therefore took place during the check of the young man.
The checks then continued along the route taken by the criminals. Inspection of the route made it possible to recover the remaining stolen goods, including the identity documents abandoned during the escape. All the recovered material was returned to its rightful owners.
The distinction is clear: the bag contained the goods stolen from the woman, while the rest of the items taken were recovered along the route. The latter also included the identity documents, left behind during the escape. The return covered all the recovered stolen goods and returned the clothing, personal belongings and documents to the owners of the van.
The officers' work therefore involved both checking the young man and inspecting the route. These are the two steps described that led to the return of the stolen goods, with the material found returned to its rightful owners. ## The legal follow-up After the arrest carried out by the Carabinieri officers, the 21-year-old accused of improper robbery was transferred to Como Prison by order of the Judicial Authority.
The subsequent investigation, however, concerns the accomplice who managed to flee. Investigations continue to identify him. The person being sought is the second fugitive intercepted near the Lido di Villa Olmo, the one who managed to escape by climbing over the facility's fence.
The two men held the 21-year-old to the ground until the prompt arrival of the Carabinieri officers. The accomplice, however, managed to flee, and investigations now aim to identify him. The detained young man was then transferred to Como.
The accomplice is therefore the person at the center of the inquiries continuing after the arrest and transfer of the 21-year-old. The case remains split between an arrest followed by transfer to Como Prison and a search that is still under way. The two developments are those indicated at the end of the operation: the 21-year-old's destination and the investigations to identify the accomplice who managed to flee.

## TL;DR - Pedemontana warns of fake toll charges via e-mail, SMS and WhatsApp - The messages threaten blocking or administrative seizure - Any tolls should be checked only on pedemontana.com - Call center: 800 936 360 ## Key facts - Who → Autostrada Pedemontana Lombarda - Where → Lombardy motorway section - Channels → e-mail, SMS and WhatsApp - Official portal → pedemontana.com - Toll-free number → 800 936 360 - New threat → vehicle block or administrative immobilization In Varese, Autostrada Pedemontana Lombarda reported a new phase of the fake toll scam. The company that manages the Lombardy motorway section says that the fraudulent messages, already circulated in recent days, have become more aggressive: they arrive via e-mail, SMS and WhatsApp and now also evoke the risk of vehicle block or administrative immobilization. Pedemontana is monitoring the phenomenon and informing customers. The central clarification is unequivocal: the company never requests toll payments through SMS or e-mails containing links to make the payment. ### The scam's new tactic According to the company's recent findings, compared with the initial attempts, the scammers have made the texts more credible and increased the pressure on recipients. The message creates a false sense of urgency: if the amount is not paid immediately, the vehicle may supposedly be blocked or administratively immobilized. The source makes clear that this claim is false. The scammers constantly change the addresses included in the messages: the links lead to fake domains unrelated to the company, in an attempt to evade security filters and IT blocks. The communication may also display official logos and trademarks, which do not change its fraudulent nature. The threat, therefore, concerns more than simply paying a toll: the messages aim to steal personal data, banking information or PIN codes for credit cards. The pressure urges users to act quickly, but the company reminds them that any outstanding tolls must be verified exclusively on the official portal pedemontana.com. For any clarification, the notice invites users to contact the company's call center, available at the toll-free number 800 936 360. Pedemontana finally recommends not opening links in suspicious SMS, e-mails or WhatsApp messages and verifying payment requests through official channels. The most delicate point for anyone receiving a request is distinguishing the visual appearance from the actual procedure. Pedemontana's findings show that scammers focus precisely on the former: more credible texts, official logos and changing addresses. The element to assess is therefore not the logo, but the channel used to request payment. The company states that SMS messages and e-mails with links are not the method it uses to request toll payments. ### A changing threat, not an official procedure The comparison with the first attempts described by the company concerns how the recipient is persuaded. Recent messages add a consequence presented as imminent: the blocking or administrative seizure of the vehicle if payment is not made immediately. Pedemontana describes this scenario as false. The threat therefore serves to create pressure and does not confirm that a toll exists. There are three levels that must not be confused. The logo belongs to the visual appearance and may appear in the message. The address is the technical link and may lead to a fake domain, not traceable to the company. The sentence about the seizure is the content that seeks to speed up the decision. Verification must remain separate from all three elements and go through the official portal indicated in the notice. The constant variation of addresses adds another difficulty. According to Pedemontana, the links change in an attempt to bypass security filters and IT blocks. For this reason, a convincingly written text does not become trustworthy merely because it resembles a company communication. The same caution applies to official logos and trademarks, which may be used in fraudulent communications. To keep checking a request separate from other mobility expenses, costo auto pendolare is a distinct budgeting tool: it does not replace verification on the company's portal. The useful information when faced with a message is knowing which channel Pedemontana indicates for checking any tolls, rather than letting the pressure of the text guide you. The company is monitoring the phenomenon and informing its customers. Its communication therefore shifts attention from the tone of the notice to the verification procedure: the form may change, while the operational guidance remains that of the official channel. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. When a message asks for toll payment, the procedure indicated by Pedemontana is straightforward. There is no need to follow the path laid out by the sender: stop before proceeding to the link, verify the request through the official channel, and use the company’s contact details if doubts remain. ### The sequence to follow 1. Stop before proceeding to the link. If the request arrives via SMS, email or WhatsApp and contains a link for payment, do not click it. The company’s instruction applies even when the text seems credible or uses an official logo. 2. Isolate the threat. If the notice mentions a block or administrative hold in the event of immediate non-payment, bear in mind that Pedemontana describes this consequence as false. item.title: Biasca: 17-year-old arrested for stabbing near the station
item.description: ## TL;DR - In Biasca, a 17-year-old Syrian resident was arrested - Injured in the abdomen, the 21-year-old is out of danger - The main charge is attempted murder
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In Biasca, a 17-year-old Syrian resident arrested - Wounded in the abdomen, the 21-year-old is out of danger - The main charge is attempted murder - The assault took place near the station
## Key facts - Location → via Bellinzona, near Biasca station - Victim → 21-year-old Italian from Leventina - Arrested → 17-year-old Syrian residing in Riviera - Injury → serious abdominal wound - Charges → attempted murder; alternatively, grievous and simple bodily harm - Authorities → Juvenile Prosecutor’s Office and Cantonal Police - Support → Transport Police - Outcome → the victim’s life is no longer in danger
### The incident and the arrest A 17-year-old Syrian residing in Riviera was arrested for the stabbing that occurred yesterday afternoon in Biasca, on via Bellinzona, near the station. The arrest was announced by the Juvenile Prosecutor’s Office and the Cantonal Police, which identified the young man as being accused of attempted murder. Alternatively, the alleged offenses are grievous bodily harm and simple bodily harm.
The victim is a 21-year-old Italian from Leventina. During a fight, according to the initial reconstruction, he was struck with a bladed weapon and suffered a serious abdominal wound. The wound made it necessary to transport him to hospital, where the young man arrived in serious condition. Doctors later reported that his life was no longer in danger.
The authorities’ statement places the stabbing during the altercation and reports that the fight broke out for reasons that the investigation will have to establish. The initial reconstruction therefore identifies the moment of the attack, while further inquiries will have to clarify how the argument developed.
The investigations and searches carried out after the incident led to the minor’s detention, also with the support of the Transport Police. After questioning, his arrest was ordered. The sequence communicated by the investigators distinguishes the moment of detention from the subsequent measure adopted at the end of the questioning.
The official communication indicates that the investigation remains open to reconstruct the exact dynamics of the events and clarify responsibility. The case is being handled by the Juvenile Prosecutor’s Office and the Cantonal Police, while from a medical standpoint the victim is no longer reported to be in danger of death. The incident thus remains linked to the elements already made public: the fight, the abdominal wound, the transport to hospital and the arrest of the 17-year-old. ## The information that emerged and the political reaction
### Safety at stations The information gathered in the following hours adds a still partial sequence. According to our information, a woman reportedly saw two young men flee on foot immediately after the assault. This was reported while the circumstances remained subject to investigation, without an official communication clarifying the role of both people seen leaving.
In the evening, Ticinonline reported that the 21-year-old, during the rescue efforts, had reportedly managed to give the names of the assailants. The same information reported that two young men had reportedly been intercepted by the police, detained and questioned. The following morning, investigators confirmed the actual arrest of a 17-year-old.
The incident has meanwhile prompted a political response. Biasca Plr Grand Councillor Omar Terraneo filed an interpellation with the government, pointing out that in recent months there had reportedly been frequent violent incidents, assaults, altercations and situations of marked distress at railway stations and in areas near the main centres.
Terraneo also refers to nuisance behaviour and repeated interventions by law enforcement. In the interpellation, he argues that stations must not gradually turn into lawless zones where citizens feel unsafe or avoid passing through at certain times of day.
«The quality of life in our canton depends both on actual safety and on perceived safety».
Among the questions addressed to the government, the deputy asks whether the reported incidents really indicate a deterioration of the situation or, above all, an increase in the population’s perception of insecurity. He also asks whether the current presence of law enforcement at stations is sufficient, particularly during the evening and night-time hours.
In closing, the interpellation asks whether a cantonal plan specifically aimed at the safety of stations and the main public transport hubs should be drawn up. The political debate thus extends to checks, the presence of law enforcement and the perception of safety in places of transit, in addition to the incident that occurred in Biasca. ## Investigations still ongoing
### Lega's questions The inquiries announced by the juvenile justice authorities and the Cantonal Police are continuing with the aim of reconstructing the exact sequence of events and clarifying responsibility. No confirmation has been given regarding the possible involvement of a second young man: the press release makes no mention of it, and PolTi's communications service, when contacted, is adhering to official communications.
This leaves open one of the elements that emerged in the hours following the assault, when the presence of two young people fleeing was reported and, subsequently, news emerged of two people being intercepted, stopped and questioned. The official confirmation concerns the arrest of the 17-year-old, while the source provides no further information about a possible second person involved.
On behalf of Lega, MP and coordinator Daniele Piccaluga emphasized protecting the population, measures to prevent violence among young people and the effectiveness of checks concerning people authorized to stay in our country. One of his requests also concerns the arrested minor.
Piccaluga is asking for information about the 17-year-old and wants to know whether social services and the authorities were aware of any violent conduct on his part. The question is part of a broader set of questions aimed at clarifying the management of foreign young people within the asylum system and coordination between the authorities.
Among the aspects identified by the MP are also the resources available to the police and juvenile justice. His intervention thus places alongside the inquiries into the stabbing a series of questions about preventing youth violence, checks and the institutional management of foreign young people.
The further course of the matter remains linked to the inquiries already announced by investigators. These investigations will reconstruct the dynamics of the altercation and clarify responsibility, while official communication leaves open the question of the possible presence of a second young man and adds no information beyond the arrest of the 17-year-old.

Between December 2020 and September 2026, the cost of living increased by approximately 8.5%, while salaries received adjustments amounting to only 3%. Based on these figures, OCST, VPOD and SIT are launching a petition addressed to the State Council and the Grand Council.
The request consists of two points: making up for the failure to recognize the cost-of-living increases of previous years for public, parapublic and social-healthcare personnel, and ensuring full recovery of the cost-of-living increase from 2027 onward. As part of the debate on the 2027 Budget, the unions reiterate their opposition to the cuts and their impact on working conditions and public services.

At the center is the failure to fully recognize the cost-of-living increase for cantonal staff. According to the unions, the repercussions extend to sectors whose pay is tied to the Canton’s salary scale: EOC, nursing homes, public SACD, USI, SUPSI, OSI and numerous municipalities.

Cross-border rail traffic between Como and Switzerland will be subject to changes on four weekends between October and November 2026. The Monte Olimpino 1 tunnel will be affected by maintenance work planned by Rete Ferroviaria Italiana (RFI) and will therefore remain closed during the scheduled periods. The closure will begin at 20:20 on Friday and end at 04:20 on Monday morning.
For cross-border commuters, the time window is the first thing to check: the closure covers the specified weekend, from Friday evening until the early hours of Monday. The change affects the TILO RE80, TILO S10, TILO S40 and EuroCity services, but not in the same way. The overview therefore distinguishes between the tunnel used, stops and route limits.
### RE80, S10, S40 and EuroCity
TILO RE80 trains bound for or coming from Milano Centrale will use the Monte Olimpino 2 tunnel. Consequently, during the closure, the trains will not stop at Como San Giovanni or Como Camerlata.
An exceptional stop will be introduced at Cucciago, allowing passengers to reach or leave the Como stations by connecting to Trenord S11 trains. For the RE80 service, this is the solution planned during the closure.
TILO S10 and TILO S40, on the other hand, will have their routes shortened. They will run only to and from Chiasso. EuroCity trains to and from Milano Centrale will also be diverted via Monte Olimpino 2 and will not stop at Como San Giovanni.
These instructions apply both to services heading towards Milano Centrale and to those in the opposite direction. ## TL;DR - A 32-year-old man from Campania was reported - A 62-year-old victim was contacted on their mobile phone - A false alarm led to a bank transfer - An account containing more than 17,000 euros was seized ## Key facts - Location → Luino Carabinieri Station - Charge → fraud - Method → fake digital payments operator - Measure → preventive seizure of the bank account - Amount → more than 17,000 euros A 32-year-old man from Campania was reported by the Carabinieri at the Luino Station after a rapid investigation and is currently considered responsible for fraud against a 62-year-old Luino resident. The victim was contacted on their mobile phone by a stranger. The man presented himself as an operator for a private company specializing in digital payment services. During the call, he made the danger of potential fraudulent withdrawals from the victim's bank account seem real. That false emergency led the person contacted to make a large bank transfer to the suspect. The sequence described by the officers centers on the shift from reporting a banking risk to asking that money be transferred to the account linked to the 32-year-old. The victim then went to the Luino Carabinieri Station to report what had happened. That report led to subsequent checks on the account identified as the recipient of the bank transfer. ### From the call to the initial response The sequence described in the investigation comprises a few steps: the phone contact, the false professional identity, the warning about withdrawals, and the bank transfer. No withdrawal made directly by the caller is described; the conduct at issue concerns inducing the victim to transfer the money for his benefit. The report was filed after the bank transfer, when the 62-year-old reached the station in Luino. The 32-year-old is identified as a suspect and is currently considered responsible. The report therefore concerns the fraud allegation reconstructed by the officers, while the checks followed the trail of the account identified as the recipient of the bank transfer. ## The dynamics of fake emergencies The method described by the Carabinieri is based on a fake telephone emergency. The caller presents himself as having an identity connected to a digital payments service and introduces the issue of possible fraudulent withdrawals. In the case handled in Luino, the warning was the story presented by the stranger to obtain a bank transfer. The source reports, in fact, that the man pretended to be an employee of a private company specializing in digital payment services. The reminder from the officers concerns not only the case that has already taken place. The Carabinieri renew their appeal to all citizens to pay the utmost attention to fake telephone emergencies. The warning includes requests for money and jewelry: people must not trust anyone who, for any reason, asks for them over the phone. The same caution applies to personal data, which must not be provided to strangers. ### Guidance for citizens The officers' message also extends attention to attempted scams. The request is to contact law enforcement immediately, without waiting for the phone call to turn into actual harm. In the case of Luino, the speed with which the victim reached the Station is identified as the factor that made it possible to act quickly on the account. This is the link between the report and the subsequent investigation: a timely report enabled the Carabinieri to carry out the banking checks. The recommendations remain practical. A phone call must not become a reason to hand over money or jewelry, or to communicate personal data to a stranger. The fact that the caller invokes a company specializing in digital payments does not change the Carabinieri's invitation to remain extremely vigilant when faced with a telephone request. The recommendation is addressed both to those who have already responded to a suspicious request and to those facing an attempt that is still ongoing. The source emphasizes that contacting law enforcement is also recommended when the scam is merely attempted, not only when the bank transfer has already been made. ## The current account identified by the military In the phase following the report, immediate banking checks enabled the carabinieri to identify the bank where the current account held in the suspect's name was maintained. The outcome of the checks led to the preventive seizure of the account and the freezing of the balance mentioned in the investigation. The account had a balance of over 17 thousand euros. In recent days, the Ticino Government had stated its position on the Confederation's Trasporti '45 programme. The assessment given was that it was a step in the right direction, but insufficient to meet the Canton’s needs. The same statement expressed concern about the postponement of the Bellinzona-Locarno link. The resolution thus brings the issue to the federal level. The Ticino Parliament is asking the Federal Council not to postpone A2-A13 any further and to return it to USTRA's priorities. The source links this request to the Locarnese's lack of direct access and the Government's opposition to a postponement beyond the stated horizon. ## The issue for those traveling through the Locarnese For cross-border commuters, the news conveys a practical distinction: the debate concerns the planning of a connection, not an immediate change to the route. For anyone who, in a hypothetical scenario, has the Locarnese as their destination, the discernible point is the uncertainty of the timeframe, not a new timetable, a new construction site or an alternative road indicated by the source. The useful comparison is between the objective expressed by Parliament and the scenario challenged in the chamber. On the one hand, A2-A13 should avoid further delays and return to USTRA's priority projects. On the other, construction has been placed in a timeframe beyond 2050, perhaps no earlier than 2055. The two perspectives do not produce the same timeframe for a region that Parliament defines as Switzerland's only large region without direct access to the motorway. ### Politics is not yet a timetable The resolution is not equivalent to the construction of the project. It is a request addressed to the Federal Council and, at the same time, a political signal about the project's place among USTRA's priorities. For this reason, no opening date can be inferred from the vote: the available text does not indicate one. Nor is the Trasporti '45 program presented by the Ticino Government as a sufficient response to the Canton’s needs; the assessment is more nuanced, because the program is considered a step in the right direction but insufficient. The reference to Bellinzona-Locarno adds the cantonal dimension to the discussion. The Ticino Government had expressed concern precisely about the postponement of that connection, while Parliament focused its resolution on A2-A13. For the cross-border commuter reader, this means distinguishing between the project’s name, the venue of the request and its possible future construction. The simulatore busta paga belongs to another editorial path: the source does not address pay-related matters. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to follow the dossier The most appropriate course of action is to follow developments without attributing to the resolution effects that the source does not announce. A cross-border commuter in a similar situation could use a simple sequence, based solely on the steps reported: identify the project, distinguish the political request from its implementation, and verify the timeframe mentioned in the chamber. 1. **Identify the project.** The main reference is the A2-A13 connection; the Ticino Government's position also refers to the Bellinzona-Locarno connection. The two references should be kept as presented by the source, without adding technical details. 2. Read the request. The Ticino Parliament asks the Federal Council not to postpone the connection any further and to put it back among USTRA's priority projects. 3. Distinguish between what is hypothetical and what is certain. Beyond 2050, perhaps not before 2055, is the timeframe indicated by the Confederation as a hypothesis and challenged in the chamber; it is not a definite opening date. 4. Track the institutional follow-up. The point to verify in any updates is whether the request from Ticino is taken up at the federal level and whether the project is once again among USTRA's priorities. ### What not to add to the news story The text does not provide timetables, travel times, alternative routes, costs, construction sites or documents to submit. This method avoids confusing a resolution with a project that has already been completed. item.title: Part-time work pays less percentage-wise
item.description: In Ticino, 65% of employees work full-time (5'456 francs/month) and 35% part-time with an equivalent remuneration of 5'121 francs, that is, 335 francs less.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In Ticino, 65% of salaried workers work full-time. - Part-time work concerns 35% of salaried workers. - For the same working hours, the average gap is 6,1%. - In Switzerland, part-time work concerns 38,5% of salaried workers. ## Key facts - Source→new October report by Ustat - Data→2024 - Full-time in Ticino→65% and 5'456 francs per month - Part-time in Ticino→35% and 5'121 francs in full-time equivalent - Ticino gap→335 francs less - Comparison for the same working hours→6,1% less for part-time work - Switzerland→38,5% part-time and 7,7% gap - Motion→Evaristo Roncelli calls for an analysis by the State Council The 6,1% is the average difference that emerges, for the same working hours, between the salary of those who work part-time and that of those who work full-time. The figure is contained in the new October report by the Statistical Office (Ustat), but the analysis invites us not to stop at the percentage: when comparing only workers with similar characteristics, the differences tend to disappear. ### The 2024 picture In 2024, in the Canton of Ticino, 65% of salaried people worked full-time and earned an average of 5'456 francs per month. The remaining 35% worked part-time; their full-time-equivalent remuneration was 5'121 francs, or 335 francs less. Ustat describes a stable situation: in 2014, the difference between the two groups was very similar. ### Women, age and profile The report indicates that it is predominantly women who work part-time, often in sectors offering lower remuneration. Age also matters: part-time work is more common among the youngest and oldest age groups. The picture changes when the comparison is made between workers with similar characteristics. In that case, the differences between full-time and part-time work tend to disappear: what affects remuneration is the employee's profile, not the percentage worked. ### The comparison and the motion In the Swiss comparison, part-time work is more common, at 38,5%, and the wage gap reaches 7,7%. The trend, however, is different: since 2014, the increase in part-time wages has been more pronounced than that of full-time wages. Ustat hypothesizes that over the past decade, people with high remuneration chose part-time work, raising the average. Yesterday, in the Grand Council, the motion by Evaristo Roncelli, of Avanti con Ticino&Lavoro, was approved, calling on the State Council to analyze disposable income as work percentages vary. The motion's proponents fear that higher income and the loss of certain subsidies may leave the same amount at the end of the month. ## The percentage is not enough The aggregate figure is useful for describing the market, but it is not enough to judge the attractiveness of an individual job. A lower average for part-time work brings together people who, according to Ustat, differ in age, gender and sectoral placement. If the comparison is narrowed to workers with similar characteristics, the gap tends to shrink until it disappears. The correct question, therefore, is not only what percentage one works, but which profile is being compared. ### For those who work across the border For a cross-border worker working in the Canton of Ticino, this caution avoids an excessive reading of the figure. The available text contains no distinctions between residents and non-residents, nor a calculation referring to the G permit. The source focuses on salary and offers no information on AVS, LPP or LAMal. Nor does it address withholding tax and double taxation. These aspects, therefore, cannot be inferred from the comparison between full-time and part-time work. The passage on disposable income raises a different issue. The motion approved by the Grand Council stems from the concern that a person already employed part-time may not be incentivized to increase their working percentage: the increase in income could be accompanied by the loss of entitlement to certain subsidies, leaving the amount available at the end of the month unchanged. It is not a new salary measure described by the source, but a request for an analysis that considers working percentages, income and subsidies together. To turn the comparison into a personal assessment, readers can place the simulatore busta paga alongside Ustat's data. If the question concerns the money left at the end of the month, costo della vita Ticino vs Italia offers a second perspective, without attributing to these statistics a precision that the source does not provide. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## An operational reading The source does not establish what percentage is appropriate for each worker and does not offer an individual procedure. To use the data without attributing answers to it that it does not contain, the reader can follow four steps. 1. Start with the reference year. Use 2024 to read the snapshot of the Ticino labor market and 2014 to verify the time comparison indicated by Ustat. 2. Keep the two salary dimensions distinct. On the one hand, there is full-time work; on the other, for part-time work, full-time-equivalent remuneration. The difference of 335 francs should be read within this statistical framework. 3. Check the profile being compared. Women, age groups and sectors do not have the same weight in the composition of the groups. The report invites readers to compare workers with similar characteristics before attributing the difference solely to the percentage worked. 4. Separate salary from disposable income. The scenario concerning subsidies is why the motion calls for a specific analysis as the percentage of work varies. It should not be confused with the salary comparison prepared by Ustat. For a cross-border worker who works in Ticino, this sequence makes it possible to use the statistics as a reference without turning them into an answer about individual conditions that the source does not examine. The institutional step to follow is the analysis requested from the State Council; the available text does not anticipate any results. For a personal estimate of remuneration, use the calcolatore stipendio. *Source: [laregione.ch](https://www.laregione.ch/cantone/ticino/1955111/il-lavoro-part-time-rende-in-percentuale-meno)*
