item.title: Varese launches the WHP program of Regione Lombardia
item.description: Wednesday, October 7, 2026, from 14:30 to 16:30, the Salone Estense in Varese hosts the presentation of the WHP Program of Regione Lombardia, organized by ATS Insubria, Municipality, Confindustria and ASST Sette Laghi.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The WHP program will be presented in Varese on October 7, 2026 - Event at Salone Estense from 14:30 to 16:30 - ATS Insubria collaborates with the Municipality, Confindustria and ASST - Focus on well-being, prevention and sustainability at work ## Key facts - What → Presentation of the WHP Program of Regione Lombardia - When → Wednesday, October 7, 2026, from 14:30 to 16:30 - Where → Salone Estense in Varese - Organizers → ATS Insubria, Comune di Varese, Confindustria Varese and ASST Sette Laghi ### The event in Varese On Wednesday, October 7, 2026, Salone Estense in Varese will host the public meeting dedicated to the presentation of the WHP Program, an acronym for Workplace Health Promotion, of Regione Lombardia. The event is scheduled from 14:30 to 16:30 and will be organized by ATS Insubria in collaboration with Comune di Varese, Confindustria Varese and ASST Sette Laghi. The stated objective is to promote a culture of well-being, prevention and sustainability within companies and organizations in the area. The initiative is dedicated to good practices in corporate welfare and prevention in workplace settings and aims to provide an opportunity for discussion among institutions, businesses and professionals. The WHP Program will be presented through the practical tools made available to companies to counter behavioral risk factors and promote healthy lifestyles. These materials will be complemented by firsthand accounts from several local organizations that have already joined the network. The names mentioned include Eurojersey, Fondazione Comi Onlus and Comune di Varese itself. The Municipality therefore appears both among the parties collaborating on the organization and among the organizations invited to share their experience within the WHP network. The announced format brings together the institutional level, dialogue with the business community and the contribution of professionals, maintaining the focus on welfare and prevention practices in the workplace. The collaboration between ATS Insubria, Comune di Varese, Confindustria Varese and ASST Sette Laghi has accompanied the event from its organization onward. The venue and time have already been defined: the public meeting will be held at Salone Estense in Varese on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, starting at 14:30 and ending at 16:30. ## The promoters' voices ### Well-being, competitiveness and prevention The reasons attributed to the program emerge from statements by representatives of the bodies and organizations involved. Davide Galimberti, mayor of Varese, considers the work environment a place called upon to protect people, foster quality of life and promote a culture of well-being. Silvia Pagani, director of Confindustria Varese, instead links people's well-being to companies' competitiveness. Her position identifies environments attentive to psychophysical balance as a key element in attracting and retaining talent. The «PEOPLE» project is mentioned as part of the work through which Confindustria Varese pursues this objective. On the healthcare front, Mauro Moreno, general director of ASST Sette Laghi, emphasizes the role of the WHP Program in networking expertise and good practices. The stated aim is to build work environments that are increasingly attentive to health, through collaboration among experience and knowledge. Salvatore Gioia, general director of ATS Insubria, broadens the scope of prevention. According to the position expressed as part of the initiative, health is not built only in healthcare services, but also in the environments where people spend a large part of their day. The four statements thus highlight different aspects of the same program: protecting people, quality of life, psychophysical balance, companies' competitiveness and the sharing of expertise. Well-being is linked both to working conditions and to companies' ability to attract and retain professionals. The contribution of the leaders of local healthcare adds the dimension of integrated prevention to the corporate dimension. WHP is described as a network of good practices and expertise, while the workplace is identified as one of the places where everyday health is built. ## The afternoon program ### Tools and testimonials The afternoon includes two items mentioned in the announcement of the meeting. One concerns the operational tools available to companies, which will be presented in relation to the need to counter behavioral risk factors and promote healthy lifestyles. The other element consists of direct testimonials from local organizations already participating in the WHP Program network. Among the entities mentioned are Eurojersey, Fondazione Comi Onlus and the Comune di Varese. Their experiences will be included in the discussion planned for the initiative, without separating the presentation of the tools from the practices already adopted by the organizations that have joined the network. The Comune di Varese therefore has a dual role at the event: it is helping ATS Insubria, Confindustria Varese and ASST Sette Laghi organize it and is listed among the local organizations that will give their testimony. The presence of the other names mentioned completes the picture of the local experiences involved. The event format is that of a public meeting and an opportunity for discussion among institutions, businesses and professionals. The regional point of reference remains the WHP Program of Regione Lombardia, while the local dimension is conveyed through the initiative's partners and the organizations already present in the network. The event is scheduled to take place at the Salone Estense di Varese on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, from 14:30 to 16:30. During that time slot, the operational tools will be presented and the announced testimonials will be presented. The program thus keeps corporate welfare, prevention in work settings and the promotion of healthy lifestyles at its center, with the involvement of the entities indicated by the organizers. *Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/luoghi-di-lavoro-che-promuovono-salute-varese-presenta-il-programma-whp-di-regione-lombardia/2699623/)*

The operation involved a young foreign national who had been of legal age for only a few days. The officers were carrying out their usual duty when they noticed the man's suspicious behavior. When he saw the uniforms, the young man tried to get rid of a small bag he was carrying by throwing it on the ground. The officers immediately recovered the package. item.title: Como and Lecco: risk of losing 14 thousand workers by 2029
item.description: UIL warning: lack of housing, complex commuting and inadequate services risk driving thousands of working-age people away from the area.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - By 2029, Como and Lecco risk losing over 14 thousand working-age people - In the Como area, 54,5% of the profiles sought are impossible to find - ASST Lariana: 40 hires out of 170 nursing positions - The Tremezzina bypass is scheduled for 2031 - Who → UIL Lario, UILFP Lario Brianza and UIL Scuola Como - Area → provinces of Como and Lecco - Horizon → by 2029 - Work → 54,5% of the profiles sought in the Como area are impossible to find - Healthcare → 170 nursing positions, 40 hires; 45 positions for family and community nurses, 10 recruited By 2029, the provinces of Como and Lecco risk losing over 14 thousand working-age people. The warning was issued by UIL Lario, UILFP Lario Brianza and UIL Scuola Como, which put the attractiveness of the area at the center of the debate. A solid economy and strong demand for labor, according to the organizations, are no longer enough to persuade people to live and stay in the area. In the Como area, the signal is already measurable: 54,5% of the profiles sought by businesses are impossible to find due to a lack of candidates. ### The paradox of essential services UIL identifies the strengthening of public services as a precondition for economic development. To make Como attractive, healthcare, schools and efficient public administrations are needed. Yet the same sectors struggle to attract and retain staff. Healthcare makes the problem concrete. In the competition announced by ASST Lariana for 170 permanent nursing positions, only 40 people were hired because the ranking list was exhausted. For the 45 positions for family and community nurses, only 10 people were recruited. > «We cannot seek nurses, teachers and public-sector staff without asking ourselves where they will be able to live and how they will be able to get around» They explain it in unison: Dario Esposito, coordinator of UIL Lombardia Lario, Massimo Coppia, general secretary of UILFP Lario e Brianza, and Gerardo Salvo, general secretary of UIL Scuola Como. The sentence sums up the point of the complaint: a job offer cannot be separated from the material conditions of the area. For a cross-border commuter reading these data, the reference to the Milan-Como-Chiasso line is one of the explicit links to daily mobility: the source mentions over 26 thousand daily travelers. It does not add schedules, individual travel times or alternative routes. To stick to the documented figure and explore only the topic of connections, the mezzi pubblici del Canton Ticino are available. ### Housing, mobility and schools are not separate chapters A practical reading of the UIL complaint starts with a change of perspective. Having a job available is not enough if a person cannot find housing, manage daily travel or integrate their family into local services. This is also relevant to the cross-border commuter who views the Como area as a place to live, without turning the source into a guide to cross-border rules. The first filter is housing. Rising prices and the growth of the so-called «grey area» make finding housing an insurmountable obstacle. The source uses this term for those who cannot access public housing but cannot afford the costs of the free market. | Issue | Evidence reported | What it indicates | | Housing | Rising prices and growth of the «grey area» | Finding housing can become an insurmountable obstacle | | Mobility | More than 26 thousand travelers on the Milan-Como-Chiasso line; Como-Lecco is single-track and diesel-powered; the Tremezzina bypass is scheduled for 2031 | Complex connections weigh on daily life | | Schools and services | Educational provision and the network of personal services | An indispensable condition for the stable integration of families | The most useful point for the cross-border commuter is the coexistence of these three issues. The number of travelers shows the scale of mobility on the Milan-Como-Chiasso line, but the source does not indicate how many are cross-border commuters and does not distinguish between the different reasons for travel. The reference to the Como-Lecco line and the Tremezzina bypass likewise describes infrastructure and expected timelines, not an individual solution. To avoid misunderstandings, the scope does not include the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax revenue shares, withholding tax or double taxation: the source provides no data on these areas. Its contribution concerns a territory’s ability to retain people through housing, mobility, schools, healthcare and public administration. To supplement this reading with a housing check, you can consult costo della vita in Ticino e in Italia. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ### A four-step check The source does not propose forms, offices, or documents to submit. The possible action is therefore an assessment framework built around the issues identified by UIL, without turning territorial data into an administrative procedure. 1. Set the timeframe. Note the two time references found in the source: by 2029 for the risk of losing working-age people and 2031 for the expected completion of the Tremezzina bypass. They are not personal deadlines, but dates useful for understanding the evolution of the area. 2. Assess housing. Describe the necessary housing solution and check whether rising prices or belonging to the «gray area» represent an obstacle. The source does not provide rents, addresses, or financial thresholds: values not contained in the text must not be added. 3. Reconstruct mobility. Consider the Milan-Como-Chiasso line, the Como-Lecco connection, which is still single-track and uses diesel traction, and the Tremezzina bypass. The source points to complex connections, but does not indicate schedules, individual travel times, or alternative routes; the assessment must remain anchored to these elements. 4. Focus on schools and services. If the choice involves a family, include in the assessment the school provision and the network of personal services, identified as essential conditions for stable integration. If it concerns healthcare, school, or public administration, supplement the application with the question of where to live and how to get around. For a cross-border worker, this checklist separates the documented territorial conditions from the information the source does not provide. ## In brief - Unions demand cost of living adjustment in the 2027 Budget - Between December 2020 and September 2026, inflation rose by 8.5% - Affected salaries were adjusted by 3% - For 2027, the Government recognized 0.25% ## Key facts - Objective → recover cost of living for public, parapublic, and social-healthcare personnel - Promoters → OCST, VPOD, and SIT - Recipients → Council of State and Grand Council - Period → December 2020-September 2026 - Inflation → approximately 8.5% - Salary adjustment → 3% - Example → 5,000 monthly francs and approximately 3,500 francs in annual loss - 2027 Measure → 0.25% cost of living recognized by the Government Between December 2020 and September 2026, inflation increased by approximately 8.5%, while the salaries of affected employees were adjusted by only 3%. This is the data on which the three Ticino unions, OCST, VPOD, and SIT, base their petition addressed to the Council of State and the Grand Council. The request is included in the 2027 Budget: to recognize the cost of living adjustment not granted in recent years and to compensate for the actual inflation of 2027. To track the impact of these items, you can also consult the cost of living, without attributing data to the tool different from those reported in the source. ### Who is included in the claim The claim directly concerns cantonal personnel. The text mentions EOC, nursing homes, public SACD, USI and SUPSI, OSI, and numerous Municipalities. The union document quantifies the effect with a case already indicated in the source: someone earning 5,000 francs monthly can suffer a loss of approximately 3,500 francs per year. The petition adds that the discrepancy is not exhausted by the adjustment of a single year. A lower salary remains so throughout a career, impacts subsequent increases, and reduces pension contributions. For 2027, the Government recognized only 0.25% for the cost of living. Read the salary situation relative to the interval between December 2020 and September 2026. The petition compares an 8.5% inflation with a 3% adjustment for the affected salaries. The case of 5,000 francs monthly and an annual loss of about 3,500 francs is the numerical reference provided by the source, not a result to be automatically applied to every worker. 3. item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Entry tax of up to 4 thousand francs for employees and self-employed workers - Switzerland votes against 900 million annually for cross-border workers - The roundtable on health tax and double taxation was on September 17 - 120 million at risk for border municipalities ## Key facts - Entry tax → up to 4 thousand francs - Allowance for unemployed cross-border workers → 900 million francs - Interministerial roundtable → September 17 - Average salary in Switzerland → 5.500 francs more in one year - Border municipalities → 120 million at risk - Legacy cross-border workers → data transmitted for the first time Up to 4 thousand francs for employees and self-employed workers: this is the item that opens the page on cross-border workers. The opening headline asks who pays it, without adding any further answer in the available material. Alongside this item is Switzerland's no to the 900 million francs per year intended for cross-border workers. ### From health tax to tax rebates The same roundup lists a tax bonus for those who spend in Ticino and, on another level, the interministerial roundtable of September 17 devoted to health tax, double taxation and status. The sequence thus connects workers, taxation and relations between Italy and Switzerland, but leaves the individual headlines distinct. The transfers section concerns border municipalities: the decree on the funds due to the administrations appears to have been signed. The page places alongside this news the item on the allowance for unemployed cross-border workers, described as a sum of 900 million charged to Switzerland, with the clarification that Switzerland can say no. The list also includes the risk of 120 million for municipalities bordering Switzerland. Regarding the health tax, the headlines record a conflict between the Ticino government, the Swiss government, Regione Lombardia, and Italian and Swiss trade unions. One speaks of a possible halt to ristorni; another calls the stoppage a violation of the agreements. After 912 days, the unions are still attacking and maintain that the health tax is a tax, not a contribution. > “The health tax is a tax, not a contribution” The salary-related thread completes the picture. Pre-filled tax returns allegedly revealed protected data about cross-border workers' salaries, with accusations of privacy violations and demands for compensation. Another headline reports 5.500 francs more in one year for the average salary in Switzerland, approaching 100 thousand. Finally, the section on legacy cross-border workers mentions an error in the data, an Irpef alert and the transmission of that data for the first time. For a cross-border worker who works in the Canton of Ticino, the first practical distinction is between the income-tax line and the political debate over tax rebates. Tax on employment income is withheld at source only in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit in section CE of form 730. This mechanism alone is not equivalent to a decision on the health tax. ### Dates and categories that change the reading The New Cross-Border Workers Agreement was signed on 23 December 2020 and has been in force since 1 January 2024. Therefore, the expression new 2026 tax agreement should not be used to indicate the effective date of that agreement. The distinction between old and new cross-border workers changes the tax-free allowance: | Item | Verified rule | |---|---| | Old cross-border workers | Already in that category before 17 July 2023; €7'500 exemption; transitional regime 2024–2033 | | New cross-border workers | €10'000 tax-free allowance | The Convention on double taxation between Italy and Switzerland dates from 9 March 1976, and Switzerland is not an EU/EEA member. These are reference points that help avoid confusing the tax reference with the rest of the issues that appear in the overview. The cross-border worker must also keep the G permit, AVS, LPP and LAMal separate: they are distinct matters from the calculation of withholding tax, the health tax and tax rebates. The tax aspect must then be checked in dichiarazione dei redditi, while AVS e LPP and LAMal do not replace checking the income tax assessment. This separation prevents every item in the Italy-Switzerland relationship from being read as if it were a deduction from the salary. ### Four checks before doing the math The figure of up to 4mila francs appears in the headline as an entry tax for employees and self-employed workers. It must therefore not automatically be turned into a personal withholding: the headline specifically raises the question of who pays it. The verification must start from the nature of the item, not only from the amount. 1. Start from July 17, 2023. Anyone who was already a cross-border worker before that date belongs to the group of old cross-border workers; the indicated transitional regime covers the period 2024–2033. For new cross-border workers, the verified allowance is €10'000. 2. If the doubt concerns employment income, separate the withholding tax deducted in Switzerland from the tax credit in section CE of the 730. Do not add the two items together as if they were the same tax. 3. If the health tax appears, treat it as a question separate from double taxation and from ristorni. The headlines in the roundup in fact show a discussion about its nature, alternatively described as a tax or contribution, and a conflict over the blocking of transfers. 4. If the check concerns the cross-border-worker headline, use the reference to permesso G/B without confusing it with the tax calculation. If instead you are reading a salary figure, consider the extra 5.500 francs as a figure referring to the average salary in Switzerland, not as an automatic increase in your payslip. This sequence makes it possible to distinguish status, income, healthcare and transfers without attributing to the individual worker figures that the source refers to categories or averages. To turn the salary figure into an estimate of net pay, use calcolatore fiscale. *Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/argomento/frontalieri/#)*

item.title: Unemployment stable at 3% in Switzerland in September 2026
item.description: In September, unemployment in Switzerland remains at 3% and in Ticino at 2,9%, with 4'800 unemployed, while job vacancies rise to 44'200.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Swiss unemployment at 3% in September. - Ticino at 2,9%, with 4'800 unemployed. - In Switzerland, 140'500 registered with the URCs. - Announced vacancies are 44'200.
## Key facts - National rate → 3% in September. - Ticino → 2,9% in September. - Grisons → 1,1% in September. - ILO comparison → 4,9% in the second quarter. - Registered with the URCs → 140'500.
Swiss unemployment stood at 3% in September, unchanged from August and July. SECO reported that, at the end of the year's ninth month, 140'500 unemployed people were registered with the regional employment offices (URCs): 1'100 fewer than in August and 7'200 more than a year earlier. Absolute figures are rounded to the nearest hundred for ease of reading. Over twelve months, however, the national rate rose by 0,2 percentage points.
In January 2021, at the most critical point of the pandemic, nearly 170'000 people without work had been recorded, with the rate at 3,7%. For those who live near the border and work in the Canton of Ticino, this comparison provides a general measure of the market in which they operate; section disoccupazione frontalieri should, however, be kept separate from SECO's official figure.
### The Ticino figure in the Swiss context
In Ticino, the rate stood at 2,9% in September, unchanged from August and up by 0,3 percentage points year-on-year. From Airolo to Chiasso, there were 4'800 unemployed: 100 more than in the previous month and 400 more than a year earlier. Ticino ranks 11th among the territories most affected by the problem; Geneva and Vaud are experiencing greater difficulties.
The Grisons recorded a rate of 1,1%, unchanged from the previous month and down by 0,1 percentage points year-on-year. In the canton whose capital is Chur, there were 1'200 unemployed, unchanged. The Grisons rank fifth among the least affected territories, led by Appenzell Innerrhoden.
The statistic has a precise scope. It counts people actually registered with the URCs and does not include those who have exhausted their entitlement to benefits and live, for example, on savings or welfare. The definition therefore differs from that of the International Labour Organization (ILO), which is based on surveys: in the latest available figure, referring to the second quarter, Swiss unemployment according to the ILO was 4,9%. ## The differences that matter to those who work across the border
A cross-border worker observing the labor market in Canton Ticino must start from the measured population. People registered with the URC are a different group from people seeking employment: the latter includes, in addition to registered unemployed people, workers attending retraining or further-training courses, participating in employment programs, or earning an interim income. Last month, people seeking employment numbered 227'600, up 0,2% compared with August.
For a cross-border worker, this marks an editorial boundary: the bulletin measures unemployment, not issues such as the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates and withholding tax. These elements should not be inferred from the percentages published by SECO.
### Age, nationality and duration
The age brackets show three distinct figures: 3,3% among young people aged 15 to 24, 3,2% among 25- to 49-year-olds and 2,6% among over-50s. The breakdown by nationality instead indicates 2,1% for Swiss nationals, unchanged month on month and with +0,1 year on year, and 5,1% for foreign nationals, unchanged month on month and with +0,2 year on year.
Another signal concerns the duration of the job search. The long-term unemployed numbered 25'600, 0,1% more than in August and 25,4% more than twelve months earlier; among them were 10'300 people over 50. The figure therefore adds to the monthly snapshot a measure of the length of registration with the URC.
The number of vacancies announced at placement offices was 44'200, with 500 more than in the previous month and 6'800 more than in the previous year. Anyone who wants to pair the statistic with a search for opportunities can consult the annunci lavoro, keeping overall availability and their own situation separate.
Short-time work also has a different reference period: in June, the latest available figure, it concerned 840 people. In September, by contrast, 3'000 people exhausted their entitlement to unemployment insurance benefits.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## A procedure for reading the next update
When SECO releases a new overview, a cross-border worker can use five simple checks. The goal is not to place on the same footing indicators based on different populations or periods.
### Five practical checks
1. **Set the period**: indicate whether the data concern September or June, as in the case of short-time work, for which the most recent information was available. 2. Identify the indicator: distinguish the percentage rate, the number of people registered with the URCs, people seeking employment, and the ILO survey. 3. Note the comparison: record whether the change is monthly or annual, because the source presents both readings. 4. Check the territory: distinguish the Swiss figure from those for Ticino and the Grisons before making comparisons. 5. Complete the form: add, when available, age group, nationality, length of registration, job vacancies, and short-time work.
The first check prevents directly comparing data referring to different months. The second reminds us that the number of people registered with the URCs does not coincide with all people seeking employment, while the ILO figure comes from surveys and has a different definition.
The third step serves to avoid confusing a change relative to August with a change over twelve months. The fourth prevents automatically attributing to the Canton of Ticino a figure referring to Switzerland as a whole. Finally, the form must indicate that absolute figures are rounded to the nearest hundred and that some values, such as job vacancies or short-time work, have a specific time frame.
To turn this reading of the labor market into a personal estimate of your paycheck, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Fines and sentences: conversion into community service in Ticino
item.description: 97 cases in Ticino in 2025. In Zurich, 1'388 requests: 4 hours of work are worth 1 day in prison.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In 2025 in Ticino: 97 conversions of sentences or fines. - In Zurich, 1'388 requests in the Infopoint's first year. - Four hours of work count as one day of imprisonment. - The success rate of the Zurich model is between 75 and 80%. ## Key facts - What → community service instead of a fine or sentence - Eligible sentences → up to six months in prison - Ratio → 4 hours of work equal 1 day in prison - Minimum commitment → at least 8 hours a week - Requests in Zurich → 1'388 - Success rate → 75-80% - Available companies → almost 250 - Ticino in 2025 → 97 cases ## The situation in Zurich and Ticino In 2025, 97 people in Ticino converted sentences or fines into community service. In previous years, based on the available data, the figure hovered around one hundred. The exception was 2024, with 125 cases. This figure runs counter to what was observed at national level, where a decline had been recorded compared with 2023. ### A voluntary option In Zurich, a foundation was established last year to promote the option offered by the justice system of performing community service instead of paying a fine or serving a sentence. The choice must come from the person concerned: there is no automatic process, and not all sentences allow recourse to this solution. Fines, monetary penalties and sentences of up to six months in prison can be converted. The source cites speeding, driving under the influence and using public transport without a valid ticket, an issue that those travelling in Ticino can explore further in the guide to trasporti pubblici in Ticino. In the event of reoffending, fines can quickly become very high, and the person is not always able to pay them. The alternatives indicated are prison or conversion. The ratio established by the model is precise: four hours of work in a hospital, even washing dishes, correspond to one day of imprisonment served. At least eight hours must be completed each week, while also complying with a series of rules for the sentence to be considered served or the fine paid. The option has existed for some time and was strengthened in 2007 with the entry into force of the new Swiss Criminal Code. After an initial increase and a period of stability, recourse to this solution declined in 2019; in German-speaking Switzerland, the reduction reported was one third. Zurich responded by intensifying promotion and creating the Fondazione Infopoint. In its first year, the new model received 1'388 requests, about 40% more than in the previous period, also thanks to leaflet distribution and plain language. Community service was granted to practically everyone who requested it. ## The practical reading for those who work across the border For a cross-border worker, this news should be kept separate from questions concerning the G permit, AVS, LPP and LAMal. The source does not cover withholding tax, tax revenue transfers or double taxation: its scope is fines, sentences and community service activities. For those who travel for work, the relevant point is limited to the examples cited: the text does not set out special rules for cross-border workers. ### The choice is not an automatic discount Conversion replaces the required service; it does not cancel the sanction. If the sentence is among those eligible, the person may choose to work instead of paying or serving time in prison; access is not automatic. Personal willingness comes first, while the hours and rules of the program determine whether the sentence will count as served. For those who use a car on their commute, speeding and driving under the influence are the road-related examples in the source. costo auto pendolare remains a separate issue, however: here the point is the legal consequence and the possibility of replacing it with an activity, not calculating travel expenses. The same criterion applies to public transport without a valid ticket. ### What the Zurich results show The first year of Fondazione Infopoint offers an operational perspective. The increase in requests was linked to distributing flyers and using easy language; almost all the people who contacted the service were given the opportunity to carry out an activity in the public interest. The success rate, however, remained between 75 and 80%: making a request does not mean that the program succeeds. Almost 250 companies throughout the Canton offer placements. When difficulties arise, counselors support people to prevent the program from being interrupted. The source links this support to the ability to find suitable activities and maintain the process. There is also the cost to the community. The people who carried out the activities did not go to prison; they worked. For the administration, this means less bureaucratic work and savings, because one day in prison costs 240 francs. The Ticino figure remains more stable than the trend observed in German-speaking Switzerland, but the source does not automatically transpose the organizational model described for Zurich to Canton Ticino. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## The operational steps described by the source The procedure can be read as a sequence of checks. The text concretely describes the Zurich model and, for the Canton of Ticino, provides the annual count. The following steps therefore illustrate the mechanism described for Zurich, without automatically attributing it to the Canton. ### 1. Start with the willingness The first condition is personal. The person must want to choose community service: there is no automatic placement. In the account of Zurich, the Infopoint Foundation was created to promote this possibility. ### 2. Verify the type of conviction The second step is to distinguish between the permitted sanctions and the others. The source includes fines, monetary penalties and sentences of up to six months in prison. It also mentions speeding, driving under the influence and using public transport without a valid ticket. Not all types of conviction allow conversion. ### 3. Measure the commitment required The substitution requires a measurable commitment: four hours of activity correspond to one day in prison and at least eight hours must be completed each week. The other program rules must still be followed. Only in this way can the sentence be considered served or the fine paid. ### 4. Identify the activity and manage difficulties In the Zurich model, one can work, for example, in a hospital washing dishes. Almost 250 companies spread throughout the Canton make jobs available. If difficulties arise, counselors support the person to prevent the program from being interrupted; the stated success rate is between 75 and 80%. ### 5. Distinguish the Ticino figure from the Zurich procedure For Ticino, the source records 97 people in 2025, around one hundred in previous years and 125 in 2024. The operational procedure described, however, is that of Zurich: the Ticino figure measures the use of the solution, while the organizational steps concern the Zurich model. The point is not merely to find a job. Success depends on the combination of a suitable activity, weekly attendance and compliance with the rules; the source specifically links the possibility of avoiding interruption to this management. item.title: Lipomo, Roxy's keen nose uncovers drugs: two arrests
item.description: Carabinieri operation in Albate: 111 grams of cocaine, hashish and 390 euros seized. Two Tunisian citizens arrested, a third reported.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Saturday, October 3, 2026: two arrests in Lipomo - 111 grams of cocaine seized - Roxy finds hashish and more cocaine - A third Tunisian national reported to authorities ## Key facts - Date → Saturday, October 3, 2026 - Location → municipality of Lipomo, near an apartment building - Operation → Carabinieri of the Albate Station - Support → Casatenovo Canine Unit - Seizure → 111 grams of cocaine, a precision scale and 390 euros ### The Carabinieri operation On Saturday, October 3, 2026, the Carabinieri of the Albate Station arrested two Tunisian nationals and reported one of their compatriots. The charge listed for the group was possession of narcotics with intent to distribute, acting jointly. The operation took place in the municipality of Lipomo, near an apartment building. The investigation involved the personnel of the Como Company working in coordination with support from the Casatenovo Canine Unit. The first part of the checks concerned the suspects and their cars. Searches led to the discovery and seizure of 111 grams of cocaine, a precision scale and 390 euros in cash. The sum was considered proceeds of the illegal activity. The material was found in the possession of two of the people detained, aged 31 and 26, respectively. Both were domiciled in the area between Como and Lipomo, and they were immediately placed under arrest. The sequence described therefore begins with checks on the vehicles and ends with the seizure of the substance, instrument and money. The first operation established the status of the two Tunisian nationals later arrested, while the third compatriot's case was addressed in the subsequent phase. The precision scale and 390 euros were found together with the 111 grams of cocaine during the initial searches. The reconstruction places the extension of the searches to the homes after this initial activity involving the suspects and their cars. ## The discovery in the home ### The role of Roxy The second phase of the operation shifted from the cars to the suspects' homes. It was during this stage that Roxy's keen sense of smell proved decisive. The dog is a drug-sniffing German shepherd working with the Casatenovo canine unit, the same unit that had supported the personnel of the Como Company. Thanks to its keen sense of smell, an additional quantity of drugs was discovered inside the apartment: 28 grams of hashish and approximately one gram of cocaine. The reconstruction therefore distinguishes the material found during the initial checks from that discovered during the search of the home. The apartment belongs to a third Tunisian national, 27 years old and residing in Lipomo. His situation differed from that of the two men arrested in the first phase: the twenty-seven-year-old was already subject to house arrest with an electronic monitoring bracelet. For the latter, the outcome of the intervention was a report without arrest for the same drug-dealing offense. The report links the accusation to the discovery made in the home, while attributing to the two nationals aged 31 and 26 the arrest that followed the seizure carried out from the suspects and their cars. Roxy's presence therefore characterized the home search. The dog enabled the Casatenovo canine unit to locate both the hashish and the second quantity of cocaine mentioned in the reconstruction, expanding the material seized in the operation. ## The outcomes indicated in the report The final outcome of the operation concerns three people and two different outcomes. The two Tunisian nationals, aged 31 and 26, residing between Como and Lipomo, were arrested after searches of the suspects and their cars found 111 grams of cocaine, a precision scale, and 390 euros in cash. According to the source, they were immediately handcuffed. The third case concerns the 27-year-old Tunisian national residing in Lipomo, owner of the home searched in the second phase. The find in the apartment, made with Roxy's assistance, consisted of 28 grams of hashish and about one gram of cocaine. The man was already under house arrest with an electronic ankle bracelet. A report was filed against the 27-year-old, who remained at liberty, for the same offense of drug dealing. The reconstruction therefore separates the outcome of the two arrests from that of the report, while linking the three cases to the accusation of joint possession of a narcotic substance for the purpose of drug dealing. The subsequent development indicated remains that of the intervention just described: two arrests and one report, with the searches moving from the suspects and their cars to the homes. The report adds no other stages, but establishes the role of the Casatenovo Canine Unit in the discovery made in the apartment. The report also distinguishes the locations associated with the different outcomes: for the two arrested men, the searches of the suspects and their cars; for the third, the apartment in Lipomo. item.title: Health insurance funds: 5% increase and proposals evaluated by experts
item.description: In 2027, the premium will increase by 5%. Three experts analyze the state fund, prevention and costs: in Ticino, from 2029, half of citizens could benefit from reductions.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In 2027 the national monthly premium will increase by 5% - Three independent experts assessed the proposals - LAMal administrative costs: around 4% of premiums - Prevention accounts for around 1.5% of healthcare spending ## Key facts - National increase → 5% in 2027 - Social insurance management costs in France → 3% - Healthcare expenditure financed directly in France → 97% - Management costs of private insurance in France → 21% - LAMal administrative costs → around 4% of premiums - Prevention in Switzerland → around 1.5% of healthcare spending - Savings from catalogue checks → around 150 million francs per year - Estimate for Ticino from 2029 → half of citizens with premium reductions In 2027 the national monthly premium will increase by 5%. Last week, the new increase in health insurance premiums for next year was announced. Numerous user proposals were submitted to the dialogue community; three independent experts examined them and commented on some of them. ### State-run fund and management costs A proposal envisions a state-managed health insurance fund, with subsidies for policyholders. The possible advantage indicated by users is a lower premium: without the aim of generating profits or distributing dividends, management could cost less. The comparison brought into the discussion concerns France. In social insurance, management costs are reported at 3%; 97% of healthcare expenditure directly finances medical services. For private insurance, management costs amount to 21%. The proposed conclusion is therefore that the public sector would be much more efficient. Christina Vetsch-Tzogiou, from Zurich University of Applied Sciences (ZHAW), shifts the focus, however, from profit to the cost structure. For mandatory health insurance under LAMal, health insurers may not make profits, while administrative costs represent around 4% of premiums. Cost growth depends mainly on the increase in expenditure per person treated, linked to medical progress, the growing use of services and possible overtreatment. In this assessment, a single fund would probably not solve the problem. ### Prevention and organization of care The proposals collected also call for stricter laws in the food sector, from a sugar tax to Nutri-Score, as well as a ban on highly processed products and limits on margins for healthy products. The promotion of sport and early, systematic screening activities for certain diseases are also mentioned. Cécile Grobet, from ZHAW, recalls that Switzerland allocates around 1.5% of healthcare expenditure to health promotion and prevention. In her view, a national strategy, clear objectives and an evaluation of costs and benefits are needed. The effect on premiums in the coming years would not be conclusive, but prevention could contribute in the long term to reducing the number of sick people. Igor Francetic, from SUPSI, considers monitoring specializations and specialists' remuneration a way to control volumes and prices. Revaluing primary care, on the other hand, would not necessarily make this sector more attractive to medical graduates. For readers who want to explore the insurance framework, the website provides guida LAMal. ## What this means in practice for those looking at Ticino For a cross-border commuter, the most concrete geographic reference in the source is the Canton of Ticino. The assessment related to the canton says that, from 2029, it is estimated that half of citizens could benefit from premium reductions. The figure describes the scenario for reductions, while 5% remains the national figure for 2027. This distinction changes how the news is read. The 5% concerns the national monthly premium; the estimate for Ticino instead concerns the possible distribution of premium reductions. These are two different levels: the first signals the announced increase, the second shows how broad the affected population could be. For those who work across the border, the two figures should therefore be kept separate. ### Costs, redistribution and timing | Proposal | Main lever | Indicated effect or limitation | |---|---|---| | State fund | Operation without profits or dividends | Potentially lower premiums; administrative costs of about 4% and per-person costs treated as the main growth factor | | Premium based on income | Distribution | Costs would change little, with potentially less awareness of costs; in Ticino, the issue of collection according to tax principles arises | | Prevention | Long-term horizon | It is not a definitive solution for premiums in the coming years; a strategy, objectives and an assessment of costs and benefits are needed | | Control of specialists | Volumes and prices | Control of specializations and remuneration can affect both dimensions | | LAMal catalogue | Effectiveness, appropriateness and cost-effectiveness | According to the UFSP, the checks have enabled savings of approximately 150 million francs per year; Grobet calls for more checks | The table separates five levers that may appear equivalent in the debate, but are not. The state fund concerns organization and the absence of profits and dividends; the income-based premium concerns the distribution of financing. Prevention works over the long term, while control of specializations and remuneration targets the volumes and prices of services. Verification of the LAMal catalogue, on the other hand, addresses the effectiveness, appropriateness and cost-effectiveness of the services included. For those who work across the border and follow the cost of living in Ticino, the figure to monitor is therefore not a single percentage. It is necessary to distinguish the announced increase, any reduction in premiums and the effect of the reforms. The confronto del costo della vita can complement this reasoning, without replacing the reading of the assessments reported. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to use expert assessments The news can be turned into a structured verification, without assigning the proposals any additional amounts or rules. For a cross-border worker following the issue in Canton Ticino, it is useful to separate the national figure, the possible reduction in premiums and structural reforms. ### A five-step method 1. Fix the national figure. Write 2027 and a 5% increase in your worksheet. Use it as an editorial starting point, not as an individual calculation: the news concerns the national monthly premium. 2. Classify the proposal. Put the state-run insurer in the management column; the income-based premium in the distribution column; prevention, specialists and the LAMal catalogue in the columns dedicated to system reforms. This separation prevents you from confusing a different distribution of costs with a reduction in them. 3. Verify which problem is being addressed. For the state-run insurer, set Christina Vetsch-Tzogiou's assessment alongside the claim that there are no profits and dividends: under LAMal, profits are not permitted and administrative costs account for approximately 4% of premiums. For the income-linked premium, record instead the assessment that costs would change little and would be distributed differently. 4. Put the proposals in chronological order. The increase figure concerns 2027; the estimate of reductions in Ticino starts in 2029; prevention is described as a long-term contribution and not as a definitive solution for premiums in the coming years. The catalogue reviews, on the other hand, have an estimated saving of about 150 million francs per year. 5. Conclude with the experts' criteria. For LAMal benefits, consider effectiveness, appropriateness and cost-effectiveness; for prevention, look at clear objectives and the relationship between costs and benefits; for specialists, observe the control of volumes and prices. A cross-border worker can thus read the Ticino figure without turning the estimate concerning half of the citizens into an individual amount. The final worksheet should keep three levels distinct: the announced fact, the expert's assessment and the possible consequence. This is a way to remain faithful to the source and not attribute an additional procedure to the reduction in premiums. To complete the check of your budget, open the calcolatore fiscale. *Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/info/dialogo/Casse-malati-i-cittadini-propongono-gli-esperti-rispondono--4135604.html)*

- What → regional conference «Fondata sul lavoro» - When → Saturday, October 10, from 9 to 18 - Where → Sala Montanari, via dei Bersaglieri 11, Varese - Organizers → Sinistra Italiana Lombardia and Alleanza Verdi e Sinistra - Path → conclusion of «Primavera del Lavoro»
## The day of discussion
On Saturday, October 10, Sala Montanari in Varese will host a day of debate and discussion promoted by Sinistra Italiana Lombardia and Alleanza Verdi e Sinistra. The regional conference «Fondata sul lavoro» will focus on wages, workplace safety, combating job insecurity and protecting purchasing power. The scheduled time for the event is from 9 to 18.
The event concludes the listening initiative «Primavera del Lavoro», developed across Lombardy to gather the concerns of workers and young people. The collection was carried out through a questionnaire prepared with the Unione dei giovani di sinistra, whose data will open the proceedings. The presentation will be delivered by provincial secretary Niccolò Minonzio, Giovanna Amodio and Luca Cappello.
The program starts at 9:30 with the questionnaire results. At 10:15, the roundtable on wages and the cost of living will bring together Bocconi historian and economist Massimo Amato, Nino Cartosio of Fiom Cgil Varese and regional councilor Onorio Rosati. At 11:45, the schedule will move on to company labor disputes, with the Rsu of Electrolux, Beko, ST, Polo della cosmesi and Gruppo Siae.
### The afternoon
At 14, the discussion will address safety and combating job insecurity, with Paolo Borghi, Enzo Mingione of Democratizing Work Italia, Stefano Ruberto of Cgil Milano and AVS senator Tino Magni. At 15:30, contracts and representation will be discussed with representatives of Cgil Lombardia, Uil Lombardia, Cisl Lombardia, Cub and Federico Martelloni of the national secretariat of Sinistra Italiana. The closing remarks, scheduled for 17, will be delivered by Tino Magni. ## From the questionnaire to labor disputes
The structure of the conference sequences three levels of discussion: the collection of demands, the discussion of general labor issues, and direct listening to companies in crisis. It is an approach that starts with data from the regional questionnaire, moves through wages and the cost of living, and arrives at the disputes brought forward by the Rsu. The program does not anticipate the questionnaire's numerical results: it only indicates that they will be presented at the opening.
### A precise scope
The political part is entrusted to the assessments of Tino Magni and Onorio Rosati. Magni describes the current situation through frozen contracts, involuntary part-time work, and cut-rate contracts. Rosati, on the other hand, stresses the need to outline an alternative proposal to the regional government's policies for the next ten years. The source thus connects the discussion both to working conditions and to the outlook for regional planning.
The section on the five companies in crisis brings the discussion from the general level to the experiences of the Rsu. The program provides no details on the individual disputes, nor does it indicate outcomes, figures, or decisions for Electrolux, Beko, ST, Polo della cosmesi and Gruppo Siae. The available information is their direct participation in the 11:45 session.
For the cross-border worker, the limits of the news must remain clear: the source provides no operational guidance on permit G, AVS, LPP, LAMal, ristorni or withholding tax. The 11:45 session is devoted to company labor disputes and includes the direct participation of the Rsu of Electrolux, Beko, ST, Polo della cosmesi and Gruppo Siae. In the afternoon, the block at 14 addresses safety and precariousness; the one at 15:30 is devoted to contracts and representation. The conclusion at 17 with Tino Magni closes the program.

item.title: Tre Valli Varesine 2026: times, route and closures
item.description: October 6: start from Busto Arsizio, finish on Via Sacco at Varese. Six city laps for men and women.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - On Tuesday, October 6th, both Binda races will take place - Women's race starts at 9:15 AM from Busto: finish expected between 12:25 PM and 1:00 PM - Men's race starts at 1:00 PM: finish expected between 5:20 PM and 6:00 PM - Six city laps for both races ## Key facts - Event → 6th Tre Valli Women's Race and 105th Tre Valli Varesine - Start → Busto Arsizio - Finish → Varese, via Sacco - Women's race → start 9:15 AM, finish between 12:25 PM and 1:00 PM - Men's race → start 1:00 PM, finish between 5:20 PM and 6:00 PM - City circuit → six repetitions - Men's long lap → two loops up to Gavirate ### The day's schedule On Tuesday, October 6th, Busto Arsizio and Varese will be the two focal points of the 105th Tre Valli Varesine, preceded on the same day by the 6th Tre Valli Women's Race. Both Binda races start from Busto Arsizio and finish in via Sacco, in Varese. The program begins in the morning with the women's race. The women start at 9:15 AM from via Volta, with the finish expected between 12:25 PM and 1:00 PM. Following the women's race, at lunchtime, it is the turn of the men's classic: the men start at 1:00 PM and are expected to finish between 5:20 PM and 6:00 PM. The temporal distinction is therefore clear. The first race occupies the morning slot, while the second begins at 1:00 PM and continues until the expected conclusion in the late afternoon. The day thus brings together two competitions with the same general starting point and the same finish, but with separate start times and finish times. ### Closures during the passage The sporting calendar is accompanied by a series of road closures along the route. The source notes that roads reopen after the last passage of the cyclists in the affected section. Reopening is therefore linked to the actual transit of the race at that point, after the group has completed the scheduled passage. The end of the transit is indicated by the 'End of race' signal, displayed on some vehicles closing the group. This is the reference point for recognizing when the cyclists' passage in the affected section ends and when the road closure can be lifted. This signaling accompanies the traffic management planned for the two Binda races. Thus, October 6th is described as a day with two distinct moments: first the women's Tre Valli, then the 105th men's Tre Valli Varesine. For both, the general start is set in Busto Arsizio and the finish is expected in Varese, via Sacco, while the transit along the course determines the closures and subsequent reopening of the roads. ## The route between Busto and Varese ### The shared route The two races share a long part of the route. After the start from Busto Arsizio, the group crosses a substantial part of the city and heads toward Solbiate and Fagnano Olona. The route then continues through Cairate, Castelseprio, Carnago, Caronno Varesino, Morazzone, Gazzada Schianno and Buguggiate. From Buguggiate, the race reaches Varese via the SP1, the provincial road along the lake. The route then includes the climb of the Ronchi and the passage through Casbeno, before the first finish on via Sacco. This passage marks the entry into the city circuit that both races must tackle in the shared part of the race. The loop in Varese includes piazza Montegrappa and via Veratti. The group then rides the first section of viale Aguggiari, passes through Montello and continues along via Marzorati-Brunella. The route continues on via Sanvito, via Campigli, via Trentini and via Daverio, then turns onto via Macchi to reach the Schiranna roundabout. From the roundabout, the route enters via Corridoni, on the climb of the Ronchi. The race then returns to via Daverio, crosses piazza Liberta and via XXV Aprile, before rejoining via Sacco. The sequence of roads defines the city circuit designated for the women's Tre Valli and the men's classic. ### The six city laps The city circuit is repeated six times by both the women and the men. The repetition includes the entire loop with piazza Montegrappa, via Veratti, the first section of viale Aguggiari, Montello, via Marzorati-Brunella, via Sanvito, via Campigli, via Trentini, via Daverio, via Macchi, the Schiranna roundabout, via Corridoni, piazza Liberta, via XXV Aprile and via Sacco. After the six laps on the city streets, the men's race adds a different part of the route. The men must in fact tackle the long circuit, extending as far as Gavirate, twice. The split from the city circuit occurs after the Montello climb, when the group descends from Casbeno-Bobbiate toward the lake. ### The men's long lap From the lake, the riders follow the SP1 to Oltrona di Gavirate. Here they tackle the Cinque Piante climb up to Barasso. The return toward Varese passes through Luvinate and Casciago, with a new return to the lake and the repeat of the Ronchi climb. The men ride this long lap twice. The men's race therefore combines the six laps of the city loop with the two additional laps that unfold between the lake, Oltrona di Gavirate, Barasso, Luvinate and Casciago, before returning to the Ronchi section. ### The participants in the men's race The presentation last Tuesday at Ville Ponti enabled Binda to unveil much of the field for the 105a Tre Valli Varesine. The list stayed fairly similar until today, when the organizers released the official start list in the evening. The men's list is headed by McNulty, listed as the world champion. At the last moment, however, Evenepoel withdrew. Many champions nevertheless remain among the entrants, as the presentation dedicated to the race points out. The transition from the presentation to the official list is the follow-up announced by Binda to define the starting field. The lineup made public in the evening maintains the picture already previewed at Ville Ponti, with the change being Evenepoel's absence and McNulty's presence at the top of the list. The list of participants for the women's Tre Valli Women's Race was also made official. The women's race is therefore accompanied by an official list distinct from that of the 105a men's race, following the presentation of the competition and its entrants. The remainder of the day will be covered live by VareseNews. The editorial team will use the same liveblog that hosted, action after action, the 107a Coppa Bernocchi. The race ended in Legnano with Frenchman Noa Isidore's victory. The live coverage will follow Binda's two races as they unfold. The liveblog is thus identified as the space chosen to accompany the cycling day, from the women's race to the men's classic, with coverage of the competition's developments. The announced coverage adds to the information already made public about the starting lists. On the one hand are the official lists, with McNulty leading the men's field and Evenepoel's withdrawal; on the other is the live coverage of the races, entrusted to the same space that covered the Coppa Bernocchi won in Legnano by Noa Isidore. *Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/guida-alla-tre-valli-varesine-percorsi-chiusure-e-corridori-al-via/2698591/)*

item.title: Bellinzona: merger and 2026 budget compared
item.description: 2025 spending of 235,8 million and 2026 budget of 253,5 million: a look at the costs of the merger.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In 2017 thirteen municipalities became a single City - The promise was greater efficiency and fewer duplications - In 2025, expenditure amounted to 235,8 million and the deficit to 2,7 - In 2026, the budget provides for 253,5 million in expenditure ## Key facts - Merger → 2017: 13 municipalities into a single City - Initial increase in salaries → approximately 3,37 million, equal to 4,7% - 2025 expenditure → 235,8 million francs - 2025 net investments → 25,4 million francs - 2026 budget → 253,5 million in expenditure, deficit of 9,17 million In 2017, Bellinzona changed its face: thirteen municipalities became a single City. Almost ten years later, Elio Del Biaggio proposes stopping the discussion of intentions and measuring the results. The promise was clear: greater efficiency, rationalization, better services, greater investment capacity, and an administrative structure suited to a larger territory. The question concerns not only projects or population growth, but also costs, taxation, services, efficiency, maintenance, and economic development. ### The rationalization challenge The main organizational argument was duplication. Thirteen administrations could have partly duplicate and unnecessary structures and functions. The single City was supposed to consolidate responsibilities, eliminate overlaps, and make better use of staff, streamlining it where necessary. The analysis, however, describes a different outcome: the old structures would have been combined without any real reduction. The result is therefore a larger municipality, but not necessarily a more efficient and less costly one. Already in the initial phase, a comparison of the budgets showed an increase in total salaries of approximately 3,37 million francs, equal to 4,7%. It was the start-up phase, and the figure alone perhaps did not demonstrate a genuine failure. But the requested assessment remains concrete: how much did the merger actually cost, and what structural savings did it produce? The issue also concerns the relationship between staff and services. A modern administration needs competent and motivated people, but the problem arises when new positions and responsibilities do not lead to a proportionate improvement in services. In 2025, the City recorded 235,8 million francs in expenditure, closing with a deficit of 2,7 million, and made 25,4 million in net investments. For 2026, the budget rises to 253,5 million in expenditure, with an expected deficit of 9,17 million. ### From project to service The question of the success of the aggregation cannot be resolved by looking only at the City’s new size. The useful comparison is between what should have changed and what the citizen encounters every day: a neighborhood, a street, a sidewalk, a service, a response from the administration or a tax to pay. Before 2017, the critical point identified by the analysis was the thirteen administrations and their possible overlaps. After unification, the assessment instead concerns the ability to truly reduce structures, duplications and costs. If the old organizations are simply placed side by side within a larger Municipality, the aggregation may change the form without automatically producing greater efficiency. | Area | Promise of the aggregation | Verification indicated by the source | |---|---|---| | Structures | Consolidate responsibilities and eliminate overlaps | How many functions have been consolidated? | | Staff | Make better use of staffing levels and rationalize them | How many positions have been eliminated or created? | | Services | Offer a proportionate improvement | How are services, roads, sidewalks and responses changing? | | Costs | Reduce structures, duplications and expenses | How much does the municipal apparatus cost today compared with the past? | This framework shifts the judgment from the organizational chart to concrete experience. An increase in salaries is not enough, on its own, to demonstrate a failure; likewise, a new responsibility does not by itself demonstrate an improvement. The figure to look for is the relationship between resources employed and services actually perceived. In the available text, the scope remains clearly defined even for the cross-border commuter reader: G permits, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax or double taxation are not examined. The verifiable object is the City’s machinery, with its expenses, taxation, maintenance and services. To keep the public account separate from the personal budget, one can consult the costo della vita. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ### A five-step reading procedure The source already offers a useful sequence for checking whether the aggregation has kept its promises, without adding assumptions unrelated to the available figures. 1. Establish the basis for comparison: in 2017, thirteen municipalities became a single City. This is the starting point for assessing organizational change. 2. Isolate the start-up phase: the comparison of the budgets indicated an increase in total salaries of approximately 3.37 million francs, equal to 4.7%. 3. Read the 2025 result: 235.8 million francs in expenses, a deficit of 2.7 million and 25.4 million in net investments. 4. Focus on 2026: the budget rises to 253.5 million in expenses and forecasts a deficit of 9.17 million. 5. Check the structure: the final check concerns positions eliminated and created, merged functions, the cost of the municipal administration and the relationship between new responsibilities and services. The fifth step is the one that connects the figures to everyday life. Indeed, the source invites readers to look beyond the organizational chart: citizens live in a neighborhood, travel on roads and sidewalks, use services, wait for responses and pay taxes. Higher costs, bureaucracy or postponed maintenance therefore make precise questions necessary, not generic assessments. To keep the value expressed in francs distinct from the currency comparison, comparatore CHF/EUR is available. The reading of the City's accounts nevertheless remains separate from the individual calculation of salaries. To move from the general figures to your own budget, use calcolatore stipendio. *Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/rubriche/ospite/1954889/servizi-costi-aggregazione-citta-domanda-bellinzona-successo-elio-biaggio)*

## TL;DR - Lereti works began on Monday, October 5, on via Copelli - Replacement of 400 meters of piping planned - Alternating one-way traffic controlled by a traffic-light system - Indicative completion: November 27, barring unforeseen circumstances ## Key facts - Work: renewal of the water supply network - Section: from the roundabout with via Gorizia to km 17+117 of SP23 - Pipelines: 200 meters of supply and 200 meters of distribution - Connection: one user connection to the new pipes - Restoration: road surfacing at the end of the work ### The project's third lot Lereti's construction site for the renewal of the water supply network began on the morning of Monday, October 5, on via Copelli, in Luino. The project is part of the company's investment plan in Varesotto, designed to increase the efficiency of the water service, reduce leakage, and improve infrastructure monitoring through digitalization. The work is not an isolated intervention. It is the third lot of an overall project launched last year with the pipelines on via Gorizia. At that construction site, one kilometer of new network was laid and, in September, the final resurfacing of the asphalt was completed. The sequence now continues on via Copelli with work connected to the same investment program. The section concerned lies between the roundabout with via Gorizia and kilometer 17+117 of provincial road 23. The schedule gives November 27 as the completion date, but only indicatively: the source specifies that the timetable remains subject to any operational contingencies or weather-related problems. The project involves approximately 200 meters of supply pipeline and a further 200 meters of distribution network. It also includes connecting one user to the new pipes. Overall, the replacement covers 400 meters of pipes, in addition to excavation, connection, and the subsequent restoration of the road. item.description: In Biasca, a 21-year-old Italian citizen residing in the Leventina district was seriously stabbed: his life is in danger.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Request for assistance shortly before 15:00 - Man stabbed on Via Bellinzona in Biasca - Victim: 21-year-old Italian man residing in Leventina - The young man's life is in danger ## Key facts - Location → Via Bellinzona, Biasca - Time → shortly before 15:00 - Victim → 21-year-old man - Citizenship → Italian - Residence → Leventina district - Condition → serious, life in danger - Request → Joint Alarm Center (Cecal) - Investigations → causes, circumstances and responsibility Shortly before 15:00, the Joint Alarm Center, known by the acronym Cecal, received a request for assistance. The report concerned a man who had been seriously stabbed on Via Bellinzona in Biasca. The Cantonal Police reported this. Officers from the Cantonal Police and the Tre Valli Police responded at the scene. Tre Valli Soccorso rescuers also worked with them, providing first aid to the young man. The injured person is a 21-year-old Italian citizen residing in the Leventina district. According to the doctors, the young man is in serious condition and his life is in danger. The Cantonal Police statement did not accompany this assessment with any other clinical data. The Cantonal Police said that investigations are underway to clarify the causes, circumstances and responsibility relating to what happened. The statement also specifies that, at present, no further information will be provided. The statement makes it possible to follow the progression from the request for assistance to the presence at the scene, without providing a reconstruction of the stabbing. The request reached Cecal; officers and rescuers then arrived at the indicated location. The presence of the Cantonal Police and the Tre Valli Police is indicated by the official note. For assistance to the injured person, however, Tre Valli Soccorso is cited: its rescuers provided first aid to the 21-year-old. The source does not attribute any other duties to the various responders and does not describe any further stages of the assistance. The geographical references also remain limited. The scene of the intervention is Via Bellinzona, in Biasca; the victim is stated to reside in the Leventina district. The statement also identifies the boy as an Italian citizen. These are the available details about the person and the area involved. The clinical assessment reported comes from the doctors: the condition is serious and the young man's life is in danger. The communication adds no other medical data beyond this assessment and the first aid provided by the rescuers. The next steps indicated by the Cantonal Police consist of the inquiries already under way. The stated objective is to clarify three aspects: the causes of what happened, how it unfolded, and the responsibilities relating to the incident. The note does not anticipate conclusions on any of these aspects. At the same time, an operation has been launched to search for the perpetrator or perpetrators. The wording used by the Cantonal Police leaves both possibilities open, without providing an identity or indicating a number of people being sought. No further details are communicated on this point either. For now, therefore, the official indication remains limited to the inquiries and searches under way. The Cantonal Police specified that no further information will be provided at the moment. The note communicates neither the outcome of the search nor a reconstruction of the incident; it merely confirms which checks have been initiated and which responsibilities still need to be clarified. *Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/cronaca/ticino-italiano-21enne-trovato-ferito-dalla-polizia-rischia-la-vita-indagini-in-corso/)*
